query is the drill-down for the complete per-bucket, per-kind set.

uuid.description: The UUID of the query.

v1ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQ.description:
Which side of the diff to page: fixed and introduced are separate lists.

 - RECORD_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: The kind was not set.
 - RECORD_KIND_FIXED: Findings present on the current base but gone on the candidate (fixed).
 - RECORD_KIND_INTRODUCED: Findings absent on the current base but present on the candidate.
 - RECORD_KIND_COMMON: Findings present on both the current base and the candidate, unaffected
by the update. Taken from the current-base side (see
BaseImageFindingRecord on ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuery).

A severity bucket to page (the severity view).

 - SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED: The severity was not set.
 - SEVERITY_CRITICAL: Critical-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_HIGH: High-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_MEDIUM: Medium-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_LOW: Low-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_NONE: Findings that carry no severity level, which a finding policy can emit.
They are counted in the totals but belong to none of the buckets above,
so a caller sweeping every record has to ask for them by name.
Spec carries the request and the computed page of records.
Inputs that select the bucket and the page.

package_version_uuid.description: The scanned application image PackageVersion (same as the impact query).

records.description:
The findings for this page (all of the requested record_kind), with
reachability projected from the app image (see §3).

v1ContainerCompositionMetadata.description: ContainerCompositionMetadata is the metadata of the composition of a container image.

v1ContainerContextDiff.description: State of the context-diff suppression feature for one container scan.

baseline_package_version_uuid.description:
Baseline PackageVersion used by the last reconcile. Informational only:
the reconcile always re-resolves the baseline rather than trusting this,
since a MAIN rescan replaces the baseline PV with a new UUID.

last_reconcile_time.description:
When the reconcile pass (CLI-triggered or the periodic auto-reconcile)
last ran for this scan.

suppress_baseline_findings.description:
True once --snooze-baseline-findings has been applied to this scan; makes
the periodic finding refresh re-run the reconcile pass against the
current baseline for as long as this stays true.

v1ContainerContextDiffQuery.description:
ContainerContextDiffQuery computes, on demand, the finding delta between two
scanned container PackageVersions: typically a MAIN-context baseline scan
of an image and an alternative-context (REF) scan of a newer build of the
same image. It is a computed query in the style of
ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuery: the response is derived live from
existing Finding and PackageVersion records and is never persisted, so it
cannot go stale as findings are recomputed.

uuid.description: The UUID of the query.

v1ContainerContextDiffQuerySpec.description: Spec carries the request and the computed response.

v1ContainerContextDiffQuerySpecRequest.description:
Inputs that select the two scans being compared and shape the
computation.

baseline_package_version_uuid.description:
The scan to compare against. When unset, resolved as the same
project's MAIN-context container PackageVersion for the same image
repository as the target.

max_top_records_per_bucket.description:
Maximum number of top changed findings per list, in both the
severity and reachability groupings. Applied to each bucket's fixed,
introduced, and common lists separately. Unset defaults to 10; set to
0 to omit the inline lists (counts only, cheaper). Capped at 100; for
a full per-bucket list use ContainerContextDiffRecordsQueryService.

package_version_uuid.description:
The scan being assessed, normally the REF-context (branch/build)
scan. Its findings are the ones suppression, when requested, acts on.

v1ContainerContextDiffQuerySpecResponse.description:
Computed results: both sides' identity, shared current counts, and the
delta between them.

reachability_available.description:
True when OS reachability analysis was enabled and succeeded on the
target scan. When true, the *_reachability_counts fields are
populated; when false they are left unset and only the *_counts
severity breakdowns are returned.

v1ContainerContextDiffRecordsQuery.description:
ContainerContextDiffRecordsQuery pages through the full fixed, introduced,
or common finding list for a single bucket (one severity or one
reachability bucket), using the standard ListParameters pagination
contract. It backs each per-bucket "View more" in the diff UI, and is also
how `--snooze-baseline-findings` pages the RECORD_KIND_COMMON set to
determine what to suppress. The diff query above returns only the top-N
inline records per bucket; this query is the drill-down for the complete
per-bucket, per-kind set.

uuid.description: The UUID of the query.

v1ContainerContextDiffRecordsQueryRecord.description:
Which side of the diff to page: fixed, introduced, and common are
separate lists.

 - RECORD_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: The kind was not set.
 - RECORD_KIND_FIXED: Findings present on the baseline but gone on the target (fixed).
 - RECORD_KIND_INTRODUCED: Findings absent on the baseline but present on the target
(introduced).
 - RECORD_KIND_COMMON: Findings present on both sides, unaffected by the diff. Taken from the
target side. This is the set `--snooze-baseline-findings` pages.

v1ContainerContextDiffRecordsQuerySpec.description: Spec carries the request and the computed page of records.

v1ContainerContextDiffRecordsQuerySpecRe.description: Inputs that select the bucket and the page.

baseline_package_version_uuid.description:
The scan to compare against (same as the diff query's baseline;
auto-resolved the same way when unset).

package_version_uuid.description: The scan being assessed (same as the diff query's target).

records.description:
The findings for this page (all of the requested record_kind), with
reachability projected from the target scan.

v1ContainerDependencyLayer.description: ContainerDependency is a dependency of a container image.

digest.description:
The SHA256 digest of the layer,
where a dependency is found to be present in the container.

file_locations.description:
The locations of the files in the container,
through which the dependency is evident to be present in the container.

first_reachable_time.description: First time this dependency was determined to be reachable in an application image.

last_reachable_time.description: Most recent time this dependency was determined to be reachable in an application image.

layers.description:
Layers of the container image where a dependency is found.
This is an optional field.
It is only set when target dependency is found via container image scan.

reachable_count.description:
Number of times this dependency was determined to be reachable in an application image.
This number is used for trending and it's not meant for exact usage tracking.

runtime_files.description:
Files accessed when a dependency is called at runtime in the container image.
This is an optional field.
It is only set when the dependency is found to be used at runtime in the container image.

user_application_dependency.description: Set to true if this is a user application dependency.

v1ContainerImageUpdateOption.description: ContainerImageUpdateOption describes a single base image update candidate.

chain_id.description: Chain ID for the candidate image's layers.

digest.description: The SHA256 digest of the candidate image (e.g., "sha256:...").

name.description:
Full image reference including registry, repository, and tag
(e.g., "docker.io/library/ubuntu:22.04").

package_version_uuid.description: UUID of the container PackageVersion produced by scanning this candidate.

v1ContainerImageUpdateOptions.description: ContainerImageUpdateOptions groups possible base image update candidates.

update_time.description: Time when these update options were determined.

v1ContainerLayer.description: A layer of a container image.

base_layer.description: True if the layer is came through the base image otherwise false.

v1ContributorActivityQuery.description:
Computes contributor activity for the latest snapshot in a requested UTC month.
This temporary query supplements snapshots created without activity metadata.
Remove it once every retained snapshot carries that metadata.

uuid.description: An ephemeral identifier for the query.

v1ContributorActivityQuerySpec.description: Parameters and results for the monthly snapshot.

date.description: Any instant in the requested month. The month is taken in UTC.

v1ContributorActivityQuerySpecResponse.description:
Project counts are exact because they come from the snapshot breakdowns.
Contributor rows retain only the latest last_seen. Later scans can make a
historical last commit older than its true value or absent.
Identity mappings use their current values. Changed mappings can also
leave a snapshot email without a last commit.
The query assumes the default 90-day activity window.

entries.description: One result per canonical snapshot email.

snapshot_date.description: Date of the latest snapshot in the requested month.

snapshot_uuid.description: Empty when the requested month has no snapshot.

Values must be max 16384 bytes.

v1ContributorHistory.description:
ContributorHistory represents a bi-weekly snapshot of aggregated contributor data
for trend visualization. Each snapshot captures the state of active contributors
in the last 90 days at the time of the snapshot.

uuid.description: The UUID of the contributor history record.

active_count.description:
The number of unique active contributors in the last 90 days
as of the snapshot date.

breakdowns.description: Breakdown of contributor counts by different dimensions (e.g. project).

emails.description: The emails of the contributors at this snapshot.

pat_scan_required_orgs.description:
The list of source-code-host orgs that require a PAT-based contributor scan
(the default app/installation-based scans did not fully cover all contributors
for these orgs, so a PAT-based job must be run instead). Each entry carries
the org host_url together with its SCM platform so on-prem instances are
unambiguously classified.

purchased_seat_count.description: The number of seats the customer has purchased as of the snapshot date.

snapshot_date.description:
The date/time when this snapshot was taken.
This represents a bi-weekly snapshot for trend visualization.
While snapshots are generated bi-weekly, the UI will aggregate to show
one record per month for display purposes.

v1ContributorIdentityMapping.description:
ContributorIdentityMapping links a SCM login to one or more normalized commit emails for a tenant.
Data is populated from SCM APIs (e.g. App based scans or PAT-backed reports) and used to deduplicate contributors across emails.

Deterministic canonical_email (persisted in spec.canonical_email, applied on create/update only):
 1. Normalize every associated email: trim ASCII whitespace and lowercase (same rules as contributor aggregation).
 2. Deduplicate, then sort lexicographically before persisting associated_emails.
 3. If any email is a GitHub noreply address for this login (see github.com docs: USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com
    or ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com), pick the lexicographically smallest matching noreply address.
 4. Otherwise use the lexicographically smallest normalized email.

Aggregation and other readers must use spec.canonical_email as stored;
they must not re-derive a different "first" email from scan order.

uuid.description: The UUID of the contributor identity mapping record.

associated_emails.description: Normalized emails associated with this GitHub user (trimmed, lowercased, sorted lexicographically on write).

canonical_email.description: Persisted canonical email for stable counting and display (recomputed on create/update by the API server).

login.description: SCM login for this identity (natural upsert key with tenant namespace).

contributor_email.description:
The email address of the contributor.
This is the unique identifier used for upserts.
Format: email addresses extracted from git commit authors.

is_forked_project.description: Indicates whether the project is a forked project.

is_public_project.description: Indicates whether the project is a public project.

last_seen.description: The last time the contributor committed to the project at the given ref.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project that the contributor is associated with.

ref.description: The ID of the git reference the contributor was discovered from.

Information about the relationship between a root package version (importer)
and one of its dependencies.
DependencyMetadata objects are children of the root PackageVersion object and
belong to the same project and namespace as the root PackageVersion object.
They are connected to the importer project through
spec.importer_data.project_uuid, and to the dependency project through

v1DependencyRiskActivity.description:
DependencyRiskActivity checks the dependencies an event introduces (from an
install command or a manifest/lockfile edit) against Endor's vulnerability

the lookup, not from the policy config.

Skip files whose path matches one of these regexes. Applied after

Only check files whose path matches one of these regexes. Empty means every
manifest/lockfile name the check recognizes.

v1DependencyRiskActivitySeverity.description:
Severity levels, mirroring Vuln.Spec.CVSSV3Severity.Level.

 - SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED: Unset. min_cvss_severity treats this as HIGH.
 - SEVERITY_LOW: CVSS low (0.1 - 3.9).
 - SEVERITY_MEDIUM: CVSS medium (4.0 - 6.9).
 - SEVERITY_HIGH: CVSS high (7.0 - 8.9).
 - SEVERITY_CRITICAL: CVSS critical (9.0 - 10.0).

v1DepsDevPackage.description:
DepsDevPackage stores package metadata from deps.dev snapshots.
This data includes package popularity (dependents count) and age information
used for typosquatting detection and package analysis.

MongoDB Atlas Search Index Configuration:
To enable fuzzy typosquatting detection, create an Atlas Search index on this collection with:
  - Field: meta.name
    Type: string
    Analyzer: lucene.keyword (treats full package identifier as single token)
  - Field: spec.ecosystem
    Type: token
    Normalizer: lowercase
  - Field: tenant_meta.namespace
    Type: token
    Normalizer: lowercase

uuid.description: The UUID of the resource.

age_weeks.description:
Age of the package in weeks since its first release.
Used to filter out old packages in typosquatting detection.

dependents_count.description:
Number of packages that depend on this package.
Used to determine package popularity for typosquatting detection.

snapshot_time.description: The timestamp of the deps.dev snapshot this data was extracted from.

uuid.description: The uuid of the resource.

v1DismissSource.description:
Which tool created a snooze or ignore, for tooling that maintains its own
dismissals over time and must never clear one it did not create.

 - DISMISS_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED: Created by a person, or by tooling that does not maintain what it writes.
 - DISMISS_SOURCE_CONTAINER_DIFF: Created by `endorctl container diff --snooze-baseline-findings`, or by the
equivalent step of `endorctl container scan --diff`. Those commands clear
the dismissals carrying this source once the finding is no longer common
with the baseline, so no other writer may set it.

v1DistinctEntry.description:
DistinctEntry tracks uniqueness for distinct-count metrics (users, repositories).
One document per (namespace, scope, bucket, distinct_key, distinct_value).
Unique compound index enforces at-most-once counting.

uuid.description: The UUID of the distinct record.

bucket.description:
Time bucket for the distinct scope. Null for all-time.
Truncated timestamp for time-bucketed aggregates (hourly, daily, weekly).

bucket_granularity.description:
Granularity of the time bucket this entry backs, as the BucketGranularity
enum name (e.g. "BUCKET_GRANULARITY_DAILY"). Set only for bucketed markers
so hourly and daily stay disjoint at midnight where both buckets are
00:00:00. A StringValue (not the bare enum) so all-time inventory markers
leave it nil: a nil wrapper serializes to null (matching pre-field docs),
keeping their unique key stable, whereas an unset enum serializes to
"...UNSPECIFIED" under EmitUnpopulated and would split the key.

distinct_key.description: Which distinct-count metric this entry tracks (e.g. "user", "repository").

scope.description:
Scope identifies the counter document this entry deduplicates against.
Format: "<enum name>:<entity name>", where the enum is a DimensionKey
for aggregate scopes or an InventoryType for inventory scopes
(e.g. "DIMENSION_KEY_MCP_SERVER:github", "INVENTORY_TYPE_SKILL:my-skill").

v1EndorAgent.description:
EndorAgent is one agent in the signed catalog published by the
endor-labs-agent-kit release pipeline. Apiserver fetches the catalog,
verifies its signature, caches it in memory, and serves it read-only via
AgentCatalogService; the monorepo stores no agent code or metadata. There is
no stored row, so uuid is derived deterministically from the agent id and is
stable across refreshes.

uuid.description:
Opaque identifier, derived from the agent id (meta.name); stable across
refreshes.

authors.description: Author display names only; no PII.

v1EndorIgnoreEntry.description:
Represents a single entry in the ignore file.

EndorIgnoreEntry objects are created by the endorctl client after
reading and processing the ignore file during the git scan,
and then applied to the findings during the analytics scan.

The ignore file is either a raw list of vulnerability ids
(one per line), or a YAML file that contains a list of ignore entries,
each identifying one or more findings in a repository version.
The file is formatted manually or via the endorctl ignore command.

Each entry must specify at least the finding name or the vulnerability ID.
The more fields you provide, the more specific the ignore entry is.
I.e. if you only provide the finding name and there are multiple
findings with the same name in the same repository version,
the ignore entry is applied to all of them.
Use the endorctl ignore --finding-uuid option to automatically populate
all fields of the ignore entry based on a given finding.

uuid.description: The UUID of the object.

dependency_name.description:
Name of the dependency of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core@2.3".
Partial matches are accepted.

This corresponds to the spec.target_dependency_package_name field
of the finding object for PackageVersion findings.

extra_key.description:
Extra key for the finding that is being ignored.
For example, the finding policy UUID.
Exact matches only.

The extra key is used internally to uniquely identify findings
(along with other fields such as the parent, target, and type)
and is stored in the spec.extra_key field of the finding object.

finding_name.description:
Name of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "Potential secret leak Generic API Key: ID #3b0fbc".
Exact matches only.

Please note that finding names are stored in the meta.description
field of the finding object rather than in meta.name.
Yes, this is confusing, but there are historical reasons for this.

parent_name.description:
Name of the parent of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "com.endor.webapp:endor-java-webapp-demo@4.0-SNAPSHOT".
Partial matches are accepted.

This corresponds to the meta.name field of the parent object
pointed to by the meta.parent_uuid field of the finding object.

project_uuid.description: Project UUID.

vuln_id.description:
Vulnerability ID of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "CVE-2025-12345" or "GHSA-7rjr-3q55-vv33".
Exact matches only.

v1EndorLicense.description: EndorLicense represents a specific Endor license assigned to a tenant.

uuid.description: The UUID of an Endor Labs license.

bundle_info.description: A repeated field containing information about Endor Labs license bundles.

credits_period_start.description:
Anchor timestamp for the scan credit counting window. Set on contract
renewal. Any unused credits will be refreshed and NOT carry forwarded once the new period starts.

is_customer.description: Indicates whether the license belongs to a customer.

license_info.description:
An array that stores the types of valid feature licenses and their
limits. Protobuf does not allow enums to be the key of maps. Ensure that
any code accessing this array checks for an existing type before writing.

read_access_until.description:
Optional. Indicates the time upto to which users of this tenant have read
access.

salesforce_account_id.description:
Salesforce Account ID for CRM integration.
Links this license to a Salesforce account for revenue attribution and
customer success reporting.

Format: Salesforce IDs are either 15 or 18 characters:
- 15 chars: case-sensitive alphanumeric (0-9, a-z, A-Z)
- 18 chars: 15-char ID + 3-char case-safe checksum
Pattern validates format only, not checksum correctness.
Ref: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9742913/validating-a-salesforce-id

scan_credit_grants.description:
History of additional scan credit buckets outside the bundle entitlement granted to the tenant, in the
order they were applied. Entries are appended via ServiceRequest by CS
when customers buy additional credits beyond the bundle entitlement.

scan_credit_limit.description:
Scan credit limit available to the tenant for the current counting
window. Computed by the backend as the derived base from seats and
bundle tiers plus the sum of scan_credit_grants. Clients must not
set this field; any value provided on write is discarded.

target_namespace.description: Target namespace of the Endor Labs license.

write_access_until.description: The time upto to which users of this tenant have write access.

v1EndorTarget.description:
EndorTarget determines the origin of the files that will be analyzed by a
rule.

v1EndorctlRC.description:
Endorctl return codes.

 - ENDORCTL_RC_SUCCESS: Success (translates to exit code 0).
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ERROR: Unspecified error.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_INVALID_ARGS: Invalid input.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ENDOR_AUTH_FAILURE: Endor API authentication failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DOCTOR_FAILURE: Endor host-check failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GITHUB_AUTH_FAILURE: GitHub authentication failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ANALYTICS_ERROR: Error running analytics.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_FINDINGS_ERROR: Error generating findings.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_NOTIFICATIONS_ERROR: Error generating notifications.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GITHUB_API_ERROR: Error calling GitHub API.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GITHUB_PERMISSIONS_ERROR: Insufficient GitHub token permissions.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GIT_ERROR: Error while performing a Git operation.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEPENDENCY_RESOLUTION_ERROR: Error during dependency resolution.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEPENDENCY_SCANNING_ERROR: Error during dependency scanning.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CALL_GRAPH_ERROR: Error while generating call graphs.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_LINTER_ERROR: Error while running the linter scanner.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_BAD_POLICY_TYPE: A user defined policy has a policy type reserved for system policies.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_POLICY_ERROR: Error evaluating one or more policies.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_INTERNAL_ERROR: Internal error while running endorctl.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: Deadline exceeded while running endorctl.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_NOT_FOUND: Requested entity was not found.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ALREADY_EXISTS: Attempt to create an entity failed because it already exists.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_UNAUTHENTICATED: Unable to authenticate request.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_VULN_ERROR: Error related to vulnerability ingestion and processing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_INITIALIZATION_ERROR: Error related to initializing the repository.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_HOST_CHECK_FAILURE: Endor host-check failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SBOM_IMPORT_ERROR: Error importing an sbom.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_PRE_COMMIT_CHECK_FAILURE: A pre-commit check failed.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GH_ACTION_WORKFLOW_SCAN_FAILURE: GitHub action workflow scan failed.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_FILE_ANALYTICS_ERROR: Error while reading files for analytics processing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILURE: Signature verification failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_LICENSE_ERROR: The requested operation requires additional licensing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_HUGGING_FACE_ERROR: Error while running the huggingface scanner.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SAST_ERROR: Error while running the SAST scanner.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ARTIFACT_OPERATION_FAILURE: Artifact operation failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SEGMENTATION_ERROR: Error during file segmentation.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_TOOLCHAIN_ERROR: Error generating toolchains.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SANDBOX_ERROR: Error running endorctl sandbox.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_RULE_SET_ERROR: Error performing rule set operations.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SECURITY_REVIEW_ERROR: Error while running the PR security review.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CODE_API_ERROR: Error while running codeAPI.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_BASELINE_NOT_FOUND: Baseline is invalid or has not been scanned yet.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SCAN_CANCELLED: Scan was cancelled.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CLONE_ERROR: Error while cloning a git repository.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_FAILED_PRECONDITION: The server refused the request because of the current tenant state or the
supplied configuration. The error details say what the caller must correct.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_POLICY_VIOLATION: One or more, enforced, admission policy violations detected.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_POLICY_WARNING: One ore more, unenforced, admission policy violations detected.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_PR_SECURITY_REVIEW_ERROR: Deprecated: Use ENDORCTL_RC_SECURITY_REVIEW_ERROR instead.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_EXPORTER_WARNING: Warning while running the exporter. This does not prevent the main scan
from completing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CONTAINER_PROFILING_WARNING: Warning while profiling a container image.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEPENDENCY_SETUP_WARNING: Warning during dependency environment setup (e.g. truststore creation).
The scan continues with a fallback configuration but may encounter issues.

v1ErrorParsingRule.description:
ErrorParsingRule is an internal API to manage error parsing rules
and regular expressions.

Object can be propagated to child namespaces. Global objects are visible to
all namespaces.

EvaluationParameter represents an evaluation parameter.
The parameters are applied to the method before execution.
The parameters correspond to the method identified by the parent UUID.

Order of evaluation:

For system methods, parameters at the system namespace
are used first. If a tenant namespace has parameters for the
same method, they overwrite the system level parameters.

v1ExceptionReason.description:
Reasons for dismissing a finding.

 - EXCEPTION_REASON_FALSE_POSITIVE: Tool is incorrect. This is not a real issue.
 - EXCEPTION_REASON_RISK_ACCEPTED: Risk acknowledged and accepted.
 - EXCEPTION_REASON_IN_TRIAGE: Issue is actively being triaged.
 - EXCEPTION_REASON_OTHER: Other reason. Use policy description or dismiss comments to elaborate.
 - EXCEPTION_REASON_RESOLVED: Issue has been resolved. For example, a secret is no longer valid.
 - EXCEPTION_REASON_PRESENT_IN_BASELINE: The finding is also present in the baseline scan this one was diffed
against, so it is not newly introduced. Set only by container diff
tooling, never by a human.

Repository version is used to select the package versions for the export.

This is the request to the SBOM export API.
It consists of the request resource kind.
The UUID is the UUID of the resource.
The output is the format to export the SBOM.
The SBOM kind is the kind of the SBOM requested by the user. Currently we support only CycloneDx.
The meta parent_kind can take one of two values - PackageVersion or RepositoryVersion.
The Meta parent_uuid corresponds to the parent UUID of the parent kind.

Specifies the output of SBOM. (For example, JSON and XML).

 - FORMAT_XML: SBOM of XML format output.
 - FORMAT_TAG_VALUE: SBOM of Tag Value format output.

The output of the SBOM, which is a string type.

Whether to include test, dev, build, and optional dependencies in the SBOM export.

The request to the VEX export API.

Whether to include findings against test, dev, build, and optional
dependencies in the VEX export. When false (the default), findings whose

propagate.description:
Indicates whether the object should be visible in the child namespaces or
not.

Custom provider's name as given by the user.

v1FactorCategory.description:
Prioritization factors are organized into categories
based on what they capture.

 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_SECURITY_RISK: Security risk related.
 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_OPERATIONAL_RISK: Operational risk related.
 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT: Captures the enterprize context, such as critical projects.
 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_COST_OF_FIXING: Captures the effort required to fix the issue.
 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_RISK_OF_FIXING: Captures the risk of attempting to fix the issue.
 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_IMPACT_OF_FIXING: Captures the level of improvement gained from fixing the issue.
 - FACTOR_CATEGORY_FEASIBILITY_OF_FIXING: Captures how feasible it is to fix the issue.

v1FactorImpact.description:
The settings capture the impact of this factor on the decision.

 - FACTOR_IMPACT_NONE: Does not affect the priority.
 - FACTOR_IMPACT_POSITIVE: Important. Increases the priority.
 - FACTOR_IMPACT_VERY_POSITIVE: Very important. Increases the priority even more.
 - FACTOR_IMPACT_NEGATIVE: Not important. Reduces the priority.
 - FACTOR_IMPACT_VERY_NEGATIVE: Not important at all. Reduces the priority even more.

v1Finding.description:
A finding contains details of a problem that needs to be fixed.
The finding applies to the parent object, which can be one of:
Repository, RepositoryVersion, or PackageVersion.
Finding objects are connected to the project via spec.project_uuid.

uuid.description: The UUID of the object.

v1FindingCategory.description:
Finding categories loosely correspond to use cases.

 - FINDING_CATEGORY_VULNERABILITY: Vulnerability.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SUPPLY_CHAIN: Supply chain specific problem (malicious packages, typosquats).
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_LICENSE_RISK: License issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SCPM: Security posture management.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SECURITY: Generic security issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_OPERATIONAL: Generic operational issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SECRETS: Exposed secret.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_MALWARE: Malware.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_CICD: CI/CD pipeline issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_TOOLS: Tooling issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_GHACTIONS: Finding applies to a GitHub action dependency.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_CONTAINER: Finding applies to a container image.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SAST: SAST.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_AI_MODELS: AI Models.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SECURITY_REVIEW: Security review.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SCA: Software Composition Analysis issue.

v1FindingClassification.description:
Classification of the finding type. Extensible for future categories.

 - FINDING_CLASSIFICATION_SECURITY_VULNERABILITY: Security vulnerability (e.g. SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded creds).
 - FINDING_CLASSIFICATION_LOGICAL_BUG: Logical bug (e.g. null pointer, resource leak, race condition).

base_image.description:
Base image of the container image where the target dependency was
found.

has_base_layer.description:
Set to true if the target dependency was found in the base layer of the
container image.

layer_digests.description:
List of layer digests for the container image where the target
dependency was found.

v1FindingCountEntry.description:
Counts for one stage of one group.
An entry is emitted only where the group matched at least one finding, so a missing entry reads
as zero rather than as absent data.

v1FindingCountGroup.description:
Identifies a group: a set of finding-matching criteria, and a tree of stages that narrows it.
Both the criteria and the stage tree live in the backend registry, which is the only emitter of
these counts. Groups are not mutually exclusive, so a finding matching two of them would be
counted in each.

 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_UNSPECIFIED: No group has been set.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_SCA_VULNERABILITY: Findings carrying both the SCA and vulnerability categories.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_AI_SAST: Findings carrying the SAST category and the AI tag.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_SECRETS: Findings carrying the secrets category.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_CONTAINER: Findings carrying the container category.

v1FindingCountStage.description:
Identifies one step in a group's stage tree.
Each value names only the criteria that step narrows by. A stage counts what is left once its own
criteria and every criteria on its path from the tree's root have been applied, so the same stage
counts a different set in each group it appears in, and the registry's stage tree is the only
place a stage's full criteria can be read. Sibling stages fork the funnel: each narrows their
shared parent independently, and their sets may overlap.

 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_UNSPECIFIED: No stage has been set.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_TOTAL: Narrows by nothing; counts every finding matching the group's own criteria.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_NOT_IN_TEST: Narrows to findings carrying the normal tag, which marks findings outside test code.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_FIX_AVAILABLE: Narrows to findings carrying the fix available tag.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_REACHABLE: Narrows to findings carrying the reachable function tag for SCA vulnerabilities, or the
reachable dependency tag for containers.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_EXPLOITABLE: Narrows to findings with an EPSS probability at or above 1%, the threshold for exploitation in
the wild. Follows REACHABLE in every group that uses it, so it never counts an unreachable
finding.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_TRUE_POSITIVE: Narrows to findings carrying the true positive tag.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_VALID_SECRET: Narrows to findings carrying the valid secret tag, set when the secret still authenticates
against its provider.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE: Narrows to findings carrying a potentially reachable tag. Forks from the same parent as
REACHABLE, and the two branches may overlap: a finding tagged both reachable and potentially
reachable is counted in each.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_POTENTIALLY_EXPLOITABLE: Narrows by the same EPSS threshold as EXPLOITABLE, but follows POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE, so it
counts the exploitable findings on the potentially reachable branch.

v1FindingFixingPatch.description: FindingFixingPatch that can fix the finding.

v1FindingFixingUpgrades.description: Upgrades that can fix the finding.

upgrade_list.description: List of upgrades that can fix the finding.

v1FindingLog.description:
A finding log contains details of the state of a finding at the time it was
created, updated or deleted.

uuid.description: The UUID of the finding log.

v1FindingLogAggregate.description:
FindingLogAggregate stores per-day FindingLog metrics.
One document per (namespace, bucket, level).

uuid.description: The UUID of the aggregate record.

bucket_day_utc.description:
Truncated to 00:00:00Z. Any other time of day forks the unique key and
splits the day across two documents.

days_unresolved_sum.description:
Sum of days_unresolved over the findings closed in this bucket. Divided
by closed it gives MTTR. No average is stored because a stored mean
cannot re-aggregate.

approximation.description:
True if this finding is for an approximate dependency
based on the unresolved package dependencies.

days_unresolved.description: Number of days that this finding remained unresolved.

finding_categories.description: List of categories that capture the use case to which the finding fits.

finding_parent_kind.description: Finding parent object resource kind. For example, PackageVersion.

finding_parent_name.description: finding_parent_name is the name of the parent object.

finding_tags.description:
List of tags, or attributes, that describe the scope of the finding
and can be used to filter findings.

location.description: File paths or URLs where the finding was detected.

target_dependency_package_name.description:
Fully qualified name of the dependency. For example,
eco://package@version.

target_uuid.description: The UUID of the DependencyMetadata object for the dependency.

v1FindingPolicyInfo.description: Details about the policy that created the finding.

name.description: Policy name.

total_num_results.description:
The total number of results matched by the policy. This number may be greater
than the list of policy matches in the results field, which is truncated if
there are more than 5 results.

uuid.description: Policy UUID.

v1FindingRecordScope.description:
Which finding types populate the record-level fixed/introduced lists. Shared
by the impact query, the records drill-down query, and the container context
diff queries. The severity/reachability COUNT fields are always computed both
ways (all_counts and vuln_counts); this selects only which findings appear in
the record lists and, correspondingly, which totals those record views
reconcile against.

 - FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unset; treated as FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_ALL.
 - FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_ALL: All finding types. Record views reconcile with all_counts / all_changes.
 - FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_VULNERABILITY: Vulnerability findings only. Record views reconcile with vuln_counts /
vuln_changes.

v1FindingRemediation.description:
Recommended action to resolve the finding.

 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_UPGRADE: Upgrade to a later version.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_DOWNGRADE: Downgrade to an older version.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REPLACE: Replace dependency with another package.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REMOVE: Remove unused dependency.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_VENDOR: Vendor a dependency.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_IMPROVE: Make changes to improve a dependency.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REIMPLEMENT: Reimplement a dependency locally.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REVIEW: Review, no remediation to suggest
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_NOTIFICATION: Notification, there may not be any remediation
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_PIN: Pin dependency to one of the recommended versions

approximation.description:
True if this finding is for an approximate dependency
based on the unresolved package dependencies.

dependency_file_paths.description:
List of relative paths to the dependency files used to create the bom, if
applicable. This field is optional and is only set when the source code
of the package version is known. For example, for Golang it contains
go.mod and go.sum.

dismiss.description:
Set to true to exclude finding from action policies
(a.k.a. admission and notification policies).
Findings can be dismissed in bulk by exception policies
and/or individually via the snooze parameters or
the ignore file.

explanation.description: Information about why this finding is considered noteworthy.

extra_key.description:
Additional information used to create a unique finding.

In some cases we want to create multiple findings for the same
combination of parent_uuid, meta.name, and target_uuid, for example when
there are multiple vulnerabilities affecting the same dependency. By
setting different values in this field, we are able to create a unique
finding per combination of parent_uuid, meta.name, target_uuid, and
extra_key.

finding_categories.description: List of categories that capture the use case the finding fits in.

finding_tags.description:
List of tags, or attributes, that describe the scope of the finding
and can be used to filter findings.

last_processed.description: Last time the finding was processed.

latest_version.description: Latest version of dependency, if available.

location_urls.description: The URLs that correspond to the paths contained in dependency_file_paths.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project to which this finding belongs.

proposed_version.description: Recommended version of dependency if available.

reachable_paths.description:
Function paths to the vulnerable method.
Only applies to vulnerability findings.

relationship.description:
String describing the relationship to dependency,
For example, "Foo is a direct dependency of bar.", if applicable.

remediation.description: String describing the recommended remediation to fix this finding.

summary.description: A more detailed description of the finding.

target_dependency_name.description:
Dependency package name, if applicable.
This is just the name (i.e. it does not include the ecosystem or the
version).

target_dependency_native_scope.description:
Un-normalized native dependency scope from the package manager
(e.g. Maven "provided"). Empty if none.

target_dependency_package_name.description:
Fully qualified name of the dependency, e.g. eco://package@version, if
applicable.

target_dependency_version.description:
Dependency version, if applicable.
This is just the version (i.e. it does not include the ecosystem or the
package name).

target_uuid.description:
The UUID of the DependencyMetadata object for the dependency, if
applicable.

v1FindingSummaryInfo.description: FindingSummaryInfo contains some selected fields for a finding.

v1FindingTags.description:
Finding attributes.

 - FINDING_TAGS_DIRECT: Finding applies to a direct dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_TRANSITIVE: Finding applies to a transitive (indirect) dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PROJECT_INTERNAL: Finding applies to a dependency that belongs to the same project.
 - FINDING_TAGS_NAMESPACE_INTERNAL: Finding applies to a dependency that belongs to the same namespace.
 - FINDING_TAGS_REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY: Finding applies to a reachable dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNREACHABLE_DEPENDENCY: Finding applies to an unreachable dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY: Finding applies to a potentially reachable dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_REACHABLE_FUNCTION: Finding applies to a reachable function.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNREACHABLE_FUNCTION: Finding applies to an unreachable function.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE_FUNCTION: Finding applies to a potentially reachable function.
 - FINDING_TAGS_FIXABLE: Deprecated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNFIXABLE: Finding is unfixable.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PRODUCTION: Deprecated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_TEST: Finding applies to a dependency not in production code.
 - FINDING_TAGS_NORMAL: Finding applies to a normal, non-test, dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_FIX_AVAILABLE: There is a fix available for the CVE reported in this finding.
 - FINDING_TAGS_SELF: Finding applies only to the analyzed package version, there is no
dependency involved.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POLICY: Deprecated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_CI_BLOCKER: Finding caused a CI failure.
 - FINDING_TAGS_VALID_SECRET: Finding applies to a valid secret.
 - FINDING_TAGS_INVALID_SECRET: Finding applies to an invalid secret.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PATH_EXTERNAL: Finding applies to a transitive dependency that can only be reached via
external, non-OSS, project paths.
 - FINDING_TAGS_MALWARE: Finding applies to malicious package.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNDER_REVIEW: Finding applies to suspicious package under review.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PHANTOM: Finding applies to a phantom dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_EXCEPTION: Finding is exempt from action policies.
 - FINDING_TAGS_CI_WARNING: Finding caused a CI warning.
 - FINDING_TAGS_NOTIFICATION: Finding triggered a notification.
 - FINDING_TAGS_EXPLOITED: This vulnerability is known to be exploited.
 - FINDING_TAGS_DISPUTED: This vulnerability has been marked as 'disputed'.
 - FINDING_TAGS_WITHDRAWN: This vulnerability has been marked as 'withdrawn'.
 - FINDING_TAGS_FALSE_POSITIVE: This finding has been analyzed to be a false positive.
 - FINDING_TAGS_TRUE_POSITIVE: This finding has been analyzed to be a true positive.
 - FINDING_TAGS_SNOOZED: Finding has been snoozed.
 - FINDING_TAGS_AI: This finding was generated using AI.
 - FINDING_TAGS_IGNORED: Finding has been ignored via the ignore file.
 - FINDING_TAGS_SEGMENT_MATCH: Finding applies to a dependency discovered via segment-matching.
 - FINDING_TAGS_REACHABLE_BY_INCLUSION: The vulnerability is assumed reachable because the package is included;
no call path to a vulnerable function exists.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POTENTIALLY_VALID_SECRET: Finding applies to a secret that has not been validated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_INFERRED: Finding applies to this package as it was forked from an upstream package
that is vulnerable to this CVE.

current_count.description: The finding count in the current version across all severities.

reduction.description: The reduction in findings across all severities.

severity.description: The breakdown of finding information per severity level.

upgrade_count.description: The finding count in the upgrade version across all severities.

current_count.description: The finding count in the current version.

fixed_count.description: The number of total findings fixed by the upgrade.

fixed_summary.description: The findings fixed. Summary information only.

introduced_count.description: The number of total findings introduced by the upgrade.

introduced_summary.description: The findings introduced. Summary information only.

reachable_fixed_count.description: The number of reachable findings fixed by the upgrade.

reachable_introduced_count.description: The number of reachable findings introduced by the upgrade.

upgrade_count.description: The finding count in the upgrade version.

v1FunctionGraphData.description: FunctionGraphData represents a function graph data request in the system.

related_object.description: The internal value that identifies the function graph storage location.

storage_url.description: The URL to the storage location of the callgraph.

uuid.description: The UUID of the function graph.

zstd_bytes.description:
Function graph proto bytes are encoded in zstd bytes.
It is the responsibility of the caller to compress/uncompress the bytes.

v1FunctionSummaryHashesQuery.description:
FunctionSummaryHashesQuery reports which of the given segment hashes are
missing a usable function summary, of any status, at the given prompt
version or newer. Unlike FunctionSummaryQuery, which returns full summary
content and only matches usable ('ok') summaries for search consumers,
this checks bare existence so a client can skip re-summarizing a segment
already tombstoned as trivial or failed.

uuid.description: Ephemeral query identifier.

v1FunctionSummaryHashesQuerySpec.description:
Spec holds the request the caller sends and the response the server
returns.

v1FunctionSummaryHashesQuerySpecRequest.description: Request selects the segment hashes to check.

hashes.description:
Exact normalized Foiegras function segment hashes to check. A request
may contain at most 1000 hashes.

prompt_version.description: Summaries at this prompt version or newer count as present.

missing_hashes.description:
The requested hashes that do not have a summary at prompt_version or
newer, of any status.

FunctionSummaryQuery searches structured security summaries for
indexed OSS functions. Non-empty filters are combined with AND.

results.description: Results in the same order as searches.

searches.description:
Ordered independent searches. Each search combines its non-empty filters
with AND. A request may contain at most 20 searches.

uuid.description: Ephemeral query identifier.

v1Fuzzy.description:
Fuzzy is used to search for a similar string. Parameters
determine the deviation.

uuid.description: The UUID of the resource.

app_registration_url.description: The URL to register the GHE app.

base_url.description: The base URL of the GHE instance.

organization.description: The organization that will own the app.

v1GemSpec.description: GemSpec represents a configuration for the Ruby gems package manager.

password.description:
An encrypted password that must be provided by the repository owner.
Superseded by `auth`; kept only for migration, removed in a later CR.

priority.description:
The priority of the Ruby gems package manager.
Priorities are relative. If multiple package managers
have the same priority, the order between them can be random.
Lower number means higher priority.

url.description: The URL of the registry that the Ruby gems package manager must use.

user.description:
The user name to use to access this repository.
Superseded by `auth`; kept only for migration, removed in a later CR.

mask.description: List of fields to return (all fields are returned by default).

v1GetSupportedReportFormatsResponse.description: Export formats the backend supports, per report job type.

formats_by_job_type.description: Supported formats keyed by job type enum name, e.g. "JOB_TYPE_FINDINGS_REPORT".

app_id.description: The app id of the installation.

enable_full_scan.description:
enable_full_scan is a boolean value that indicates if the full scan should
be enabled.

enable_pr_comments.description:
enable_pr_comments is a boolean value that indicates if the automated PR
comments should be enabled.

enable_pr_scans.description:
enable_pr_scans is a boolean value that indicates if the automated PR scans
are enabled.

host_url.description: The base URL of the corresponding SCM app.

include_archived_repos.description:
include_archived_repos is a boolean value that indicates if the archived
repos should be included. Default will be off.

installation_github_user.title: installation_github_user is the Github user that initiated the installation

v1GitHubPRConfig.description:
GitHubPRConfig configures automated GitHub pull requests for remediations.
Deprecated: Use RemediationPRConfig, which supports all SCM platforms.

enabled.description: Turns the creation of automated pull requests on or off for this target.

v1GitHubPayload.description: GitHubPayload carries SCM-specific webhook data for a GitHub-originated scan.

pull_request_payload.description:
pull_request_payload contains the GitHub Pull Request payload
associated with this scan request, when available. This allows downstream
components (e.g., security review scanner) to avoid refetching PR data
from GitHub and instead map this JSON to internal structures on demand.

v1GitHubWorkflows.description: GitHubWorkflows Metric Value contains information about the workflow file's code posture management.

enable_full_scan.description:
enable_full_scan is a boolean value that indicates if the full scan should
be enabled.

enable_mr_comments.description:
enable_mr_comments is a boolean value that indicates if the automated MR
comments should be enabled.

enable_mr_scans.description:
enable_mr_scans is a boolean value that indicates if the automated MR scans
are enabled.

personal_access_token.description: PAT of the user doing integration to fetch resources using REST APIs.

webhook_secret.description:
The webhook secret configured in GitLab for validating incoming webhook
events.

v1GitSpec.description:
Git repository project configuration.

Fields of this object might differ from the Git host.

external_installation_id.description:
Endor Labs GitHub app installation ID of this project.
Optional and only available if the project is created through an
installation.

full_name.description:
Represents the Git namespace and its associated hierarchy.

The format is "namespace/name", comprising the organization name and
repository name.

For example, yarpc/yarpc-go

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq .full_name

git_clone_url.description:
The Git clone URL.
For example, git://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git.

The URL is stored as lower case letters to normalize searches.

http_clone_url.description:
The HTTP clone URL.

The following examples show valid URLs.

https://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git

http://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git

https://my.github.com/a/b.git

https://www.gitlab.com/a/b/c.git

https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x.git

https://github.com/jboss/jboss-ejb-api_spec.git

The URL is stored as lower case letters to normalize searches.

invalid_installation.description:
Indicates that Endor Labs installation no longer exists
for this project and was potentially deleted. Endor Labs can no longer
refresh or rescan this project.

organization.description:
The organization where the repository is located.

For example, yarpc

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq
.organization.login

path.description:
The source control repository in the project without the organization.

For example, yarpc-go

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq .name

web_url.description:
The web URL to view the repository.

For example, https://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq .html_url

The URL is stored as lower case letters to normalize searches.

app_name.description: The name of the GitHub app.

client_id.description: The client ID of the GitHub app.

client_secret.description: The client secret of the GitHub app.

html_url.description: The HTML URL of the GitHub app.

pem.description: The PEM file of the GitHub app. This is the private key of the GitHub app.

webhook_secret.description: The webhook secret of the GitHub app.

token.description: The address fields of the tenant.

v1GitlabPayload.description:
GitlabPayload carries SCM-specific webhook data for a GitLab-originated scan.
Mirrors GitHubPayload so downstream components (e.g., AI SAST baseline
lookup) can recover the originating MR number on merge-to-main webhook
events where pull_request_id is intentionally blank.

merge_request_payload.description:
merge_request_payload contains the raw GitLab merge request webhook
payload as JSON. The originating MR number lives at
"object_attributes.iid".

v1GradleSpec.description: GradleSpec represents properties that need to be set for Gradle projects.

property_key_name.description: The key name for Gradle properties.

property_key_value.description: The key value for Gradle properties.

v1GroupAggregationValueResponse.description:
GroupAggregationValueResponse returns the value of the aggregation if
requested.

v1GroupResponse.description: Response to a list group request.

v1HarnessSandbox.description:
HarnessSandbox identifies sandboxing around the agent harness itself.

 - HARNESS_SANDBOX_UNSPECIFIED: Harness sandboxing was not evaluated.
 - HARNESS_SANDBOX_NONE_DETECTED: No harness sandbox was detected.
 - HARNESS_SANDBOX_CONTAINER_DIY: The harness appears to run inside a generic container.
 - HARNESS_SANDBOX_DEDICATED_TOOL: The harness is managed by a dedicated sandbox tool.
 - HARNESS_SANDBOX_SANDBOX_RUNTIME: The harness is managed by a sandbox runtime.
 - HARNESS_SANDBOX_UNKNOWN: Checked but could not be classified.

v1Hash.description: Sequence of characters that can help you verify data integrity.

sha256.description: Checksum value of package in hash 256 algorithm.

sha512.description: Checksum value of package in hash 512 algorithm.

hdr_name.description: The name of the header field that contains the signature.

secret.description: The secret to use for the HMAC calculation.

v1HttpParam.description:
HttpParam is the key/value pair that will be rendered as "Key: Value"
in the section of the requested portion of the HTTP request. It could
be part of the request like the header, the query, or the body.

If the authz flag is set, the library will render it as
"Authorization: Key Value" instead of just "Key: Value".

authz.title:
If set, render the key-value as "Authorization: Key Value"
instead of just "Key: Value". The supported keys are the ones
specified in the Authorization enum (as string)

separator.description: The separator to use between key and value. Default is ":".

v1HttpParamsProfile.description: HttpParamsProfile defines the parameters to create an HTTP request.

allowed_template_params.title:
AllowedTemplateParams defines a list of allowed template parameter names and regexes for validating their values.
Only the template parameters with names in this list will be allowed in the template_params field.
Example: [{"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_CLIENT_ID", "regex": "abc[0-9]{3}"}, {"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_TENANT_ID", "regex": "xyz[0-9]{3}"}]

description.description: Detailed description of the request. For example, "GitHub credential validation".

name.title: Name identifies this entry. For example, "GitHub"

request_body.description:
Request body as a string. This will be sent as the body of the HTTP request.
If both request_body and the body parameter in SendRequest are provided,
the body parameter takes precedence.

template_params.title:
Template parameter values to use when required template parameters are not found
in the vicinity of the secret for validation. Each entry represents a set of values that can be
tried in sequence during validation.
Example: [{"values": [{"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_CLIENT_ID", "value": "abc123"}, {"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_TENANT_ID", "value": "xyz789"}]}]

v1HttpParamsRequest.description: HttpParamsRequest contains the information expected with the HTTP request.

body.description: The information to be put in the HTTP body.

header.description: The information to be put in the HTTP header.

method.description: Method is either GET or POST.

method_name.description:
Gets appended to the URL as:
URL[:method_name] usually followed by the query section.

query.description: The information to be put in the HTTP query section.

uri.title: The URI to use for this validation. For example, "https://api.github.com/user"

v1HttpParamsResponse.description: HttpParamsResponse contains the information expected with the HTTP response.

failed_auth_codes.description: The codes expected on the failed authentication.

invalid_code_regex.description: The pattern/regex expected on failure. For example, "5\\d\\d".

status_code.description: The code expected on success. For example, 200.

successful_auth_codes.description: The codes expected for a successful authentication.

successful_response_data.description:
Map of key-value pairs that must be present in the response body for successful validation.
This allows validation beyond just HTTP status codes.
Example: {"ok": "true", "status": "active"} would require the response to contain both keys
with matching values. The response can contain additional fields.

successful_response_text.description:
The expected response body text for successful validation.
Example: "invalid_payload" would require the response body to contain the text "invalid_payload".
The response body may contain additional text.

access_token.description:
Optional HuggingFace API token used to authenticate requests for
private models within the organization. When omitted, only publicly
accessible models are discovered.

avatar_url.description: Avatar URL of the HuggingFace organization.

uuid.description: The UUID for the ingested HuggingFace model.

author.description: Author of the model. For example, "openai".

authorization_required.description: Requires authorized request to access the model.

created_at.description: Date of creation of the repository on the Hub.

disabled.description: Whether the repository is disabled or not.

downloads.description: Number of downloads of the model.

last_modified.description: Date of last commit to the repository.

likes.description: Number of likes of the model.

mask_token.description: Mask token used by the model.

model_id.description: Author and model name (seems to hold the same value as the name field).

name.description: Author and model name (id). For example, "openai/clip-vit-base-patch16".

organization_name.description: Organization name for which this model belongs to.

pipeline_tag.description: Pipeline tag associated with the model.

private.description: Whether the repository is private not.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project that this model relates to.

sha.description: Repository SHA at this particular revision.

siblings.description: List of files that constitute the model.

spaces.description: List of spaces using the model.

tags.description: List of tags of the model.

transformers_info.description: Transformers-specific information associated with the model.

widget_data.description: Widget data associated with the model.

v1HuggingFaceOrganization.description: HuggingFaceOrganization represents a HuggingFace organization and its associated metadata.

uuid.description: The UUID for the HuggingFace organization.

model_names.description: Names of models that belong to this organization.

url.description: URL of the HuggingFace organization page.

v1IOCReviewStatus.description:
IOCReviewStatus records who established the IoC status, independent of what
that status is. Automated short-circuit decisions require human_reviewed.

 - IOC_REVIEW_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: No review stage has been set.
 - IOC_REVIEW_STATUS_PENDING_REVIEW: Newly ingested; no reviewer has looked at it yet.
 - IOC_REVIEW_STATUS_AUTO_REVIEWED: Set by an automated classifier or enrichment source.
 - IOC_REVIEW_STATUS_HUMAN_REVIEWED: Set by a human researcher.

v1IOCStatus.description: IOCStatus represents the confirmation status of an IoC.

v1IOCType.description: IOCType classifies the type of Indicator of Compromise.

v1IPAddressPolicy.description:
An IPAddressPolicy creates a restriction on which IP address subnets can
access a tenant.
Note that only one IP address policy is allowed per tenant and IP address
policies cannot be declared in child namespaces.

propagate.description:
Propagate indicates that the object should be visible in child namespaces.
It should be set to true for most use cases.

uuid.description: The UUID of the ip address policy.

allowed_ip_subnets.description:
The list of allowed IP subnets from where traffic should be
allowed.

propagate.description: Propagate indicates that the object should be visible in child namespaces.

uuid.description: The UUID of an identify provider.

v1ImportedRuleSet.description: ImportedRuleSet represents a request to import a set of rules.

uuid.description: The UUID of the object.

v1ImportedRuleSetSpec.description: The internal specification of the object.

bytes.description: A file has been used as a source.

opengrep_validate.description: Validate this import request with opengrep.

sha256_hash.description: The SHA256 checksum if applicable (e.g, file).

version.description: The version for this rule set. All rules in the set will be created with this version.

v1ImportedSBOMSpec.description: The internal specification of the object.

cyclone_dx.description: CycloneDX is the cyclonedx bom struct serialized to a string.

cyclone_dx_bytes.description: CycloneDX bom struct encoded in zstd bytes.

The unique identifer of the component of a SBOM.
For example, a CycloneDX SBOM will have metadata.component.bom-ref as the identifier of the main component.

main_component_purl.description: The PURL of the main component of a SBOM.

spdx.description: SPDX is the spdx bom struct serialized to a string.

spdx_bytes.description: SPDX bom struct encoded in zstd bytes.

supplier_name.description: The suplier name of the imported SBOM.

version.description: The version of the imported SBOM.

IndexData is used to index the resource for search. It's an internal
object.

search_score.description: search_score is the score of the resource for search. Internal use only.

will_be_deleted_at.description: Time that the resource will be deleted.

v1IngestedObject.description:
Raw ingested object from a 3rd party source,
along with any additional metadata we want
to add to the object.

ingestion_time.description: Time the object was last ingested.

v1IngestionState.description: IngestionState represents the state of data ingestion for cross-cluster communication.

uuid.description: The UUID of the ingestion state.

last_malware_ingestion_time.description: Timestamp of the last successful malware ingestion (updated by malware ingestor).

last_vuln_ingestion_time.description: Timestamp of the last successful vulnerability ingestion (updated by vuln ingestor).

v1Installation.description: Installation represents an installation request in the system.

propagate.description: Propagate indicates that the object should be visible in child namespaces.

uuid.description: The UUID of the installation.

cleanup_stale_namespaces.description:
Indicates whether stale managed namespaces that no longer correspond
to groups or projects in the SCM should be automatically deleted
during installation reconciliation. Default value is false.

enabled_features.title: Enabled features. The valid values are "git, github"

exclude_project_regexes.description:
exclude_project_regexes is a list of RE2 regular expression patterns used
to exclude repositories from ingestion during SCM integration
reconciliation. A repository is excluded if its name (leaf name only, not
the full URL or path) matches any pattern in this list. Matching is
case-sensitive. An empty list means no filtering is applied. Supports a
maximum of 20 patterns.

external_id.description: The external ID of the installation.

external_name.description: The external name of the installation.

include_archived_repos.description:
include_archived_repos is a boolean value that indicates if the archived
repos should be included. Default will be off.

ingestion_time.description: The last time that we ingested the installation data.

ingestion_token.description:
The API token that the scanner can use for scanning installation
related information. If it is empty, the scanner will use local
authentication information.

installation_error_message.description:
Message explaining why the installation is invalid.
This field is populated when invalid is true.

invalid.description:
Identifies the installations that are in the system,
but potentially their corresponding configuration has been removed
from GitHub and thus we cannot authenticate. In this case,
we stop trying to re-sync with this installation.

login.description:
The login of the account taken directly from the GitHub response
VS spec.user, which is inferred from the identity token in the request
context.

marked_for_deletion.description:
Indicates the installation is marked for deletion,
and in next sync call the installation with its related data will be
deleted.

project_uuids.description: The list of projects that are associated with this installation.

public.description: Apply only to public repositories. Default value is false.

scm_app_uuid.description: The UUID of the SCM app being installed.

suspended.description: Indicates if the installation is suspended.

target_type.description: The target of the installation (Organization or User).

user.description:
The user name of the user that initiated the installation.
Refers back to the GitHub user name.

v1InternalToolHook.description: InternalToolHook contains payload for internal tool-related hooks.

tool_input.description: Tool invocation input; structure is tool-specific (use Struct for JSON).

tool_response.description: Tool result; structure is tool-specific (e.g. stdout/stderr or filenames).

v1InventoryAdminClassification.description:
InventoryAdminClassification carries the allow/block axis plus evidence.
Within a single event, when multiple matching policies disagree, the
stronger value wins (BLOCKED dominates ALLOWED dominates UNSPECIFIED).
Across events, the current policy set is authoritative: a later event
that no longer matches any classification policy leaves the field
untouched, but a later event matching a different policy reclassifies
the record accordingly.

v1InventoryClassification.description:
InventoryClassification declares the classification a policy assigns to a
matched MCP server or skill when it fires. UNSPECIFIED means the policy
plays no role in inventory classification (e.g. a session, file-access,
or cmd-line policy, or an MCP/skill policy whose author only wants the
per-event action).

v1InventoryClassificationEvidence.description:
InventoryClassificationEvidence records the policy that assigned the
current value on a single classification axis. Snapshotted from the
matching AgentHookPolicy so the inventory record remains self-describing
after the policy is renamed or deleted.

policy_name.description: Policy name at the time of match (snapshot — not refreshed later).

v1InventoryThreatClassification.description:
InventoryThreatClassification carries the suspicious/malicious axis plus
evidence. Within a single event, when multiple matching policies disagree,
the stronger value wins (MALICIOUS dominates SUSPICIOUS dominates
UNSPECIFIED). Across events, the current policy set is authoritative:
see InventoryAdminClassification for the full semantics.

v1InventoryType.description: InventoryType discriminates agent, model, MCP server, skill, and AI tool inventory in the unified collection.

v1Invitation.description: Invitation represents an invitation for a new user in the system.

uuid.description: The UUID of the invitation.

user_email.description: The email of the user that we want to invite to the tenant.

api_key.description: The API Key to authenticate with Jira.

bearer_token.description: The bearer token to authenticate with Jira.

cloud_id.description: The Jira Cloud ID required to route API requests through the Atlassian API gateway.

components.description: The Components field in Jira board.

jira_child_issue_type.description:
Child issue type used for dependency aggregation. Optional.
Defaults to the project's sub-task type when unset.

labels.description: The labels to apply to the Jira issue.

project_key.description: The project key in which the Jira issue is raised as an action for the notification.

resolve_state.description: The final ticket status after resolving.

url.description: The Jira endpoint.

use_bearer_token.description: Denotes if we should use bearer token to authenticate with Jira.

user_name.description: The user name to authenticate with Jira.

v1JVMClassMetadata.description: JVMClassMetadata contains metadata such as file sha, name, gav of oss library for a jvm class file.

uuid.description: The UUID of the jvm class metadata.

file_name.description:
Name of java class file.
This would be the fully qualified class name, such as org.slf4j.ILoggerFactory.

gav.description:
Open source library that contains this class file, in endor ecosystem name format.
eg for org.slf4j.ILoggerFactory, this value would be mvn://org.slf4j:slf4j-api@1.7.

is_original_sha.description:
True indicates if the class file sha value is the original class's sha value.
False indicates the sha value would be for a class that is remapped, i.e namespace wiped off.

is_rebundled.description: True indicates if the class file is a dependency class file which has been rebundled within this package.

v1JVMSourceMeta.description: Contains metadata information about source code for a Java package.

classes.description: List of classes in the Java package.

import_statements.description: List of external classes referenced in the Java package.

end_time.description: End time of the job denotes the time when the job execution is completed.

last_heartbeat_time.description: Last Heartbeat time of the job.

max_duration.description: Maximum duration of the job. Defaults to 5 minutes.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries for the job. Defaults to 1. Maximum allowed is 5.

retention_time.description:
Retention time of the job. Defaults to 30 days.
Cannot exceed 1095 days.

run_errors_history.description:
run errors history of the job. This is maintained
for debugging purposes.

source_uuid.description: UUID passed back to the client for which the job is being performed.

start_time.description: Start time of the job denotes the time when the job is scheduled for execution.

unstructured_content.description: The unstructured content of the LLM context.

v1Language.description: - LANGUAGE_GOSU: Gosu, a JVM language used by Guidewire applications.

v1Languages.description: The languages used and bytes of code for each language in the source control repository.

v1LicenseData.description:
Contains a summary of license information for a project or package.
This will be included as the payload of a metric object.

all_licenses.description: All the licenses found by Endor Labs.

code_licenses.description: The licenses found in the source code.

copyrights.description: The list of copyright notices found in source files.

package_manager_licenses.description: The licenses from the package manager.

uuid.description: The UUID of the license dependency.

v1LicenseDependencyMetadata.description: LicenseDependencyMetadata contains license information for a dependency.

type.description: License classification (based on licenseclassifier by Google).

declared.description: Whether we classify the license as declared.

osi_approved.description: Indicates if the license is OSI approved.

package_version_uuids.description: Package versions of dependencies with the license.

v1LicenseFileLocation.description: LicenseFileLocation represents the location of a license, copyright, or notice in source files.

end_byte.description: The end byte of the license/copyright/notice in the file.

end_line.description: The end line of the license/copyright/notice in the file.

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file where the license/copyright/notice was found.

start_byte.description: The start byte of the license/copyright/notice in the file.

start_line.description: The start line of the license/copyright/notice in the file.

v1LicenseInfo.description: LicenseInfo contains information for a license.

file.description: The name of the file where the license was found.

file_location.description: The line in the file where the license text begins.

matched_text.description: The license text that was matched.

name.description:
Raw license description as found, for example in package managers.
It is free form text that may not contain a valid SPDX ID.

type.description: License classification (based on licenseclassifier by Google).

url.description: The URL that points to the license description.

v1LicenseMappingInfo.description:
LicenseMappingInfo contains additional information
that we determine when we attempt to match a license string
to a known SPDX id.

 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_NOT_OSS: This does not look to like an OSS license.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_IN_CODE: License information is to be found in the code.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_UNKNOWN: Cannot determine anything about the license.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_NOT_INCOMPLETE: There is some license information, but is not detailed enough.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_PRIVATE: Appears to be a private package.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_EXACT: An exact match to a SPDX id.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_UNLICENSED: Seems to be explicitly without license.

uuid.description: The UUID of the license notices report.

contents.description: The contents of the license notices report.

package_license_edit_uuid.description: Deprecated: not used by current implementations; kept for wire compatibility.

package_version_uuid.description:
UUID of the package version for which this report is generated.
Handlers should use the same propagation/merge semantics as MergedLicenseData
when assembling the effective licenses, copyrights, and notices.

v1LicenseSource.description:
Enum to describe the source of  license information.

 - LICENSE_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED: Licesne Source unspecified
 - LICENSE_SOURCE_PKG_MGR_ONLY: License was found only in the package manager metadata,
but not in the source code. This may happen if source code is unavailable
or scanning failed. In this case, spec.license_data contains only package manager license(s).
 - LICENSE_SOURCE_PKG_MGR_AND_CODE: License was found in both the code and the package manager.
spec.license_data contains all licenses, and the Metric includes the package manager license.
 - LICENSE_SOURCE_CODE_ONLY: License was found only in the code , not in the package manager.
spec.license_data will not include any package manager license.
 - LICENSE_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND: No license data found anywhere

v1LicenseSpec.description: Specification mostly follows the SPDX data format.

uuid.description: The UUID of the license summary.

copyright_count.description: The number of copyrights found in the project dependencies.

declared_spdx_ids.description: The declared SPDX IDs per license associated with the project.

notices_count.description: The number of notice files found in the project dependencies.

singular_spdx_ids.description: The singular SPDX IDs of all licenses associated with the project.

spdx_ids.description:
The SPDX IDs per license associated with the project.
This includes declared and discovered licenses.

v1LinterCorrectnessAnalysis.description: LinterCorrectnessAnalysis represents an analysis of a linter result.

analysis_summary.description: Analysis summary, providing an explanation of the linter result and classification.

code_fixes.description: Code fixes are potential fixes to the identified issue.

code_references.description: Textual description of line references/ fields/variables , etc for the linter result.

content_hash.description:
sha256 over the source spans (finding location + taint dataflow) this analysis
was computed against; a mismatch on rescan invalidates the cached verdict and
forces re-analysis of the result.

data_flow.description: Textual Description of the source to sink data flow analysis for the linter result.

description.description: The textual description of the linter correctness analysis.
