v1LlmJudgment.description:
LlmJudgment is one judgment the LLM judge made while an event was evaluated,
recorded so the cost, the latency, the label distribution and the accuracy of
the judge can be measured on real traffic rather than assumed.

It lives on the event and not on the policy match. One command is one judge
call but zero or more matches, so a record per match would duplicate and every
count run against it would double-count; and a record on the match could not
cover the commands that matched nothing, which under JUDGE_SCOPE_ALL_COMMANDS
are the majority.

ai_request_uuid.description:
Join key to the AIRequest row for this call, which carries CompletionUsage
and the credit accounting.

Cost is derived from that row and the price table of the day, never stored
here: a stored currency figure goes stale on a price change and cannot be
recomputed. Note the derived figure is a FLOOR — the hook client retries a
failed POST and each retry bills another inference, while only the attempt
that returned leaves its uuid here.

cached_tokens.description:
Tokens served from the provider's prompt cache. The rubric is a standing
prefix, so this reports whether it is actually being cached — something the
RFC's cost table assumes rather than measures.

completion_tokens.description:
Tokens the label itself cost. Small by design: a large value means the model
is explaining itself rather than answering.

confidence.description:
The model's own 0.0-1.0 self-report, advisory only: recorded so a threshold
can be calibrated against real data rather than guessed.

error.description:
Set when the judge could not be reached, timed out, or returned something
unusable. Without it a fail-open allow reads in the data as a real allow and
the fail-open rate cannot be measured at all.

judged_matches.description:
The policy matches handed to the judge, as the patterns produced them and
before the label acted on them.

This is the only record of what the judge decided against. A benign label
removes these matches from policy_matches, and a review or suspicious label
rewrites their action, so without this copy an event cannot say which policy
fired or what it would have done. Empty when the judge ruled on a command no
pattern matched, which JUDGE_SCOPE_ALL_COMMANDS does for most commands.

latency_ms.description:
Round trip as the client measured it, covering assembling the request and
mapping the answer back. The one number here that the server-side AIRequest
row cannot produce.

model.description:
The model that produced the label, as served — the backend rewrites the
requested model when aliasing or fallback applies.

reason.description:
One clause naming the concrete thing the model saw. This is also the text
the agent is shown when a judgment raises an ask or a block, which is why an
AUTO policy carries no message of its own.

rubric_version.description:
Version of the rubric the label was produced under. A label recorded today
is not comparable to one recorded after the rubric changed, which is the
whole reason the rubric is embedded verbatim rather than assembled per call.

v1LlmJudgmentKind.description:
What the judge was asked to rule on.

 - KIND_COMMAND_RISK: Risk of a shell command the agent proposed to run.

v1LogLevel.description:
- LOG_LEVEL_EMERGENCY: System is unusable, for example, a panic condition.
 - LOG_LEVEL_ALERT: Action must be taken immediately, for example, a corrupted system
database.
 - LOG_LEVEL_CRITICAL: Critical conditions such as hard device errors.
 - LOG_LEVEL_ERROR: Error conditions.
 - LOG_LEVEL_WARNING: Warning conditions.
 - LOG_LEVEL_NOTICE: Normal but significant conditions that may require special handling.
 - LOG_LEVEL_INFO: Informational messages that confirmation that the program is working as
expected.
 - LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG: Messages that contain information normally of use only for debugging.

v1MalwareAssessmentErrorStatus.description:
Status categorizes the kind of error that occurred.

 - STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: No error type has been set.
 - STATUS_RULE_EVALUATION: A detection or analysis rule failed to evaluate.
 - STATUS_DATA_UNAVAILABLE: Required input data was missing or unavailable.
 - STATUS_TIMEOUT: The assessment exceeded its time budget.
 - STATUS_LLM: An LLM call failed.
 - STATUS_INTERNAL: An internal or system-level failure occurred.
 - STATUS_UNSUPPORTED: The package or target is not supported.

v1MalwareAssessmentLLMCallStats.description: MalwareAssessmentLLMCallStats tracks LLM usage statistics for a specific model.

v1MalwareAssessmentMethod.description:
MalwareAssessmentMethod records how a verdict was reached. A short-circuited
assessment never ran the terminal LLM, so its confidence and reasons must be
read against a different bar than an LLM verdict.

 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED: No method has been set.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_LLM: Produced by the terminal LLM decision.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_IOC: Produced by a match against a known-malicious, human-reviewed IoC.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_YARA_SHORT_CIRCUIT: Produced by a YARA rule match that skipped the LLM.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_LLM_REVIEW: Produced by an LLM pass that critiqued an earlier verdict.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_MANUAL: Set by a human researcher.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_SYNC: Imported from an external feed rather than assessed here.
 - MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_IOC_SHORT_CIRCUIT: Legacy spelling of the IoC short-circuit, kept so migrated records
round-trip. Write MALWARE_ASSESSMENT_METHOD_IOC for new assessments.

v1MalwareCheckActivity.description:
MalwareCheckActivity runs Endor's malware lookup against the packages in a
package-install command (a cmd_line event). It carries no regex matchers:
matching the activity means running the check, and the block/allow verdict
comes from the malware feed (MALWARE-status, non-contested records), not from
the policy config.

aliases.description: Identifiers this malware is already known by elsewhere, for example a GHSA or OSV id.

assessment_uuid.description:
The assessment to promote. It must carry a MALICIOUS result and no assessment_error;
anything else is rejected rather than promoted.

cwe_id.description: Weakness classification the reviewer assigns, for example CWE-506.

references.description: Supporting links, such as an upstream advisory or a registry takedown notice.

summary.description:
One-line description of the malicious behaviour for feed consumers, who see the
record without access to the assessment behind it.

v1MalwareDetectionAssessmentPromotionRes.description: MalwareDetectionAssessmentPromotionResponse holds the malware record the promotion produced.

already_promoted.description: true when the assessment had already been promoted.

accepted.description: When true, a human reviewer has accepted this assessment verdict and promoted it to the internal malware feed.

assessment_duration.description: Duration of the assessment process in seconds.

change_log.description: Change log entries, ordered by changed_at for sorting.

enable_export.description: When true, assessment is eligible for advisory creation and external reporting (e.g. PyPI, OSV). Default true.

human_reviewed.description: Whether this has been reviewed by a human.

human_reviewed_reasons.description: Reasons provided when the assessment was human-reviewed.

iocs.description: IoC's of the malware observed during the assessment.

prompt_compressed.description:
Compressed prompt (zlib+base64). Legacy: only populated by assessments
written before prompts_compressed existed, or by writers that have not
migrated yet. No longer written once a writer populates
prompts_compressed; readers should treat prompts_compressed as
authoritative when both are present and fall back to this field for
older or mixed-version records where prompts_compressed is empty.

prompts_compressed.description:
Stores LLM prompts for the terminal singals.
The caller is responsible for compressing/uncompressing the bytes.

version.description: Package version.

workflow_uuid.description: UUID of the workflow that produced this assessment.

v1MalwareDetectionBinaryStringsSignal.description: MalwareDetectionBinaryStringsSignal extracts strings from binary files and passes them to an LLM for analysis.

max_strings_to_llm.description: Maximum number of extracted strings to send to the LLM.

max_tokens_to_llm.description: Maximum total tokens of extracted strings to send to the LLM per binary.

min_string_length.description: Minimum string length (in characters) to extract from binaries.

strings_timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for the strings extraction step.

max_diff_line_length.description: Maximum character length per diff line before truncation.

max_file_size_for_diff.description: Maximum file size in bytes to include in the diff; -1 means unlimited.

max_diff_line_length.description: Maximum character length per diff line before truncation.

max_diff_size_bytes.description: Maximum total diff size in bytes; -1 means unlimited.

max_file_size_for_diff.description: Maximum file size in bytes to include in the diff; -1 means unlimited.

v1MalwareDetectionDependenciesSignal.description: MalwareDetectionDependenciesSignal collects transitive dependency information for the package.

v1MalwareDetectionDownloadStatsSignal.description: MalwareDetectionDownloadStatsSignal fetches download statistics to assess package popularity.

v1MalwareDetectionGitHubSignal.description: MalwareDetectionGitHubSignal retrieves GitHub repository signals and analyzes them via an LLM.

max_commits.description: Maximum number of commits to include.

max_contributors.description: Maximum number of contributors to include.

max_releases.description: Maximum number of releases to include.

v1MalwareDetectionInstallHooksSignal.description: MalwareDetectionInstallHooksSignal inspects package install hooks (preinstall, postinstall scripts).

v1MalwareDetectionIoC.description: MalwareDetectionIoC represents an Indicator of Compromise.

uuid.description: The UUID of the IoC record.

v1MalwareDetectionIoCIngestorSignal.description: MalwareDetectionIoCIngestorSignal runs IoC and YARA short-circuit checks before the full analysis.

yara_short_circuit_enabled.description: When true, the signal exits early upon any YARA match.

yara_short_circuit_rule_prefix.description: Prefix used to identify short-circuit YARA rules, e.g. "MAL_".

change_log.description: Change log with ISO timestamp keys.

sightings rather than replaced.

filename.description: File the IoC was extracted from, relative to the package root.

first_seen_at.description:
When this IoC was first observed. Distinct from meta.create_time, which
is when this record was written and does not survive a data migration.

last_seen_at.description:
When this IoC was last observed in a package. Distinct from
meta.update_time, which also moves on edits that are not sightings.

value.description: Value of the IoC. Immutable for the same reason as type.

llm_analysis_threshold.description: Minimum number of files that must be present before LLM analysis is triggered.

context_lines.description: Number of context lines to include around each finding.

v1MalwareDetectionPackage.description: MalwareDetectionPackage represents a package in the malware detection system.

uuid.description: The UUID of the package record.

v1MalwareDetectionPackageFilesSignal.description: MalwareDetectionPackageFilesSignal reads and lists files from the package archive for downstream signals.

max_files.description: Maximum number of files to include from the archive.

v1MalwareDetectionPackageIoC.description:
MalwareDetectionPackageIoC represents a relationship between a package and an IoC.

Each side of the link gets its own message, carrying the identity of the object on
that side. Both sides can therefore be counted or grouped by the names a caller
already holds, with no lookup first. Those identities cannot drift: each one is the
unique key of the object it came from, so changing it would name a different object
and make a different link.

One object is one link. A unique index over both identities keeps it that way, so a
count of links is a count of distinct packages, or of distinct IoCs.

uuid.description: The UUID of the package-IoC relationship record.

context.description: Context describing the relationship between the package and the IoC.

version.description: Package version.

v1MalwareDetectionPackageVersionsSignal.description: MalwareDetectionPackageVersionsSignal gathers version history of the package from the registry.

max_versions_to_show.description: Maximum number of recent versions to include in the signal output.

v1MalwareDetectionSecondStageAnalysisSig.description: MalwareDetectionSecondStageAnalysisSignal downloads and LLM-analyzes files referenced by suspicious code paths.

download_timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for each individual file download.

enable_llm_cache.description: When true, previously fetched LLM responses are reused to reduce cost.

max_download_size.description: Maximum total download size in bytes across all second-stage files.

max_file_size_for_llm.description: Maximum file size in bytes to pass to the LLM.

max_files_to_analyze.description: Maximum number of files to download and analyze.

v1MalwareDetectionSignal.description: MalwareDetectionSignal defines a single analysis unit within a signal group.

capture_iocs.description: IoC types this signal is expected to capture; order reflects capture priority.

depends_on.description: Names of signals that must complete before this signal runs; execution order follows the declaration order of this list.

is_terminal.description: When true, this signal produces the terminal verdict for the group.

keep_temp_files.description: When true, temporary files written by this signal producer are not deleted after execution; useful for debugging.

name.description: Name that uniquely identifies this signal instance within the workflow.

output_template.description:
Go template that overrides the default go output template for this signal.
When set, the scanner uses this template instead of the built-in template to render
the signal's structured output into text before passing it to the LLM decision signal.
Template variables must match the signal producer's output model; unrecognised variables
are treated as empty strings.

v1MalwareDetectionTyposquattingSignal.description: MalwareDetectionTyposquattingSignal detects potential typosquatting by comparing the package name to known packages.

similarity_threshold.description: Minimum similarity score (0.0 – 1.0) to flag a package as a potential typosquat.

v1MalwareDetectionWorkflow.description: MalwareDetectionWorkflow stores a named scan workflow configuration used by the malware detection pipeline.

uuid.description: The UUID of the workflow record.

capture_iocs.description: IoC types this workflow is expected to capture across all signal groups; acts as a workflow-level default.

disabled.description: When true, malware detection is disabled for this workflow.

infer_mal.description:
When true, only the primary registry mirror is checked and shortcut verdicts produce MALICIOUS;
when false all mirrors are searched and shortcut verdicts produce UNKNOWN.

is_default.description: When true, this workflow is selected by default when no explicit workflow is requested.

signal_groups.description: Execution order of signal groups; groups are run in the order they appear in this list.

v1MalwareDetectionYaraSignal.description: MalwareDetectionYaraSignal scans package files with YARA rules to identify malware patterns.

context_lines.description: Number of context lines to include around each YARA match.

max_file_size_mb.description: Maximum file size in megabytes to pass through YARA scanning.

show_code_snippets.description: When true, matching code snippets are included in the signal output.

v1MalwareExposure.description:
Namespace exposure for a given Malware package.
The presence of this object indicates that at least one project in the
Namespace is, or was, potentially affected by the referenced Malware.
If all affected projects are in child namespaces, then there are no
MalwareExposure objects in the parent namespace. Use traverse to
include MalwareExposure objects from child namespaces.
The meta.name field contains the fully qualified package name of the
Malware package. For example, "npm://package-name".

uuid.description: UUID of the MalwareExposure object.

v1MalwareExposureQuery.description: Request to get the exposure of one or more Malware objects on a given namespace.

uuid.description: UUID of the MalwareExposureQuery object.

filter.description:
String of conditions to filter MalwareExposure objects by.
For example, to only get data for the last 7 days, use:
"meta.create_time >= now(-168h)".

Only applied if malware_uuids is empty.
Skips contested malware records.

Note: The filter is applied to the MalwareExposure objects,
not the Malware objects.

Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

malware_uuids.description:
UUIDs of the Malware objects to get exposure for.
Leave empty to get exposure for all, non-contested Malware objects.
Use the filter field to get exposure for a subset of Malware
objects if you do not have the UUIDs.

Note: The UUIDs are not checked for existence.
There is no error returned if a UUID is not found, but there
will not be an entry for it in the project counts.

project_uuid.description: Limit the request to a specific project.

traverse.description: Get data from any child namespaces as well.

v1MalwareExposureQuerySpecResponse.description:
Response data for MalwareExposureQuery.

Contested malware records are skipped unless explicitly requested
via the malware_uuids field.

definitely_affected_projects.description: List of definitely affected project UUIDs.

malware_counts_by_project.description: Malware counts per project, indexed by project UUID.

potentially_affected_projects.description: List of potentially affected project UUIDs.

project_counts_by_malware.description: Project counts per Malware object, indexed by Malware UUID.

malware_detected_on.description:
Date the malware was detected in public repositories.
Copied directly from the malware record, so that it
can be used to filter MalwareExposure objects.

Format: 2017-01-15T01:30:15.01Z
RFC 3339: https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt.

v1MalwareIOCAttribute.description:
MalwareIOC represents a particular Indicator of Compromise.
Use it to embed the IOC attributes in other messages.

v1MalwareMatch.description:
MalwareMatch describes a package flagged by the malware check. The verdict
comes from a MALWARE-status, non-contested record in Endor's malware feed.

reasons.description: Why the package is flagged — indicators reported by the malware feed.

source.description: Feed that flagged it, as the MalwareSource enum name (e.g. "MALWARE_SOURCE_AMF").

summary.description: Short title from the malware feed (e.g. "Malicious code in <pkg> (npm)").

version.description: Version from the install command, when it was pinned; empty for an unpinned install.

v1MalwareSignalGroup.description: MalwareSignalGroup is an ordered collection of signals that execute together.

name.description: Name that uniquely identifies this group within the workflow.

signals.description: Ordered list of signals in this group.

additional_notes.description: Additional notes for the malware record.

advisory_last_updated.description: Timestamp of the last update of the malware record by the advisory.

advisory_published.description: Date when the advisory published the malware record.

contested.description: Has the malware record been contested.

contested_date.description: Date when the malware record was contested.

contested_reason.description: Reason for the malware record being contested.

contributing_feeds.description:
Feeds that contributed to this record. Set on merge when more than one
source applies; each value is a concrete feed (not UNSPECIFIED). Empty
when a single feed supplies the record or provenance is not tracked.

cwe_id.description: The CWE ID for the malware record.

deletion_exempt.description:
When true, this record is exempt from orphaned malware deletion and will never be
automatically removed during ingestion cleanup, regardless of whether it was ingested.

iocs.description: IOC attributes of the malware found during the analysis.

malware_detected_on.description: Date when the malware was detected.

pkg_release_date.description: Release date of the package version.

purl.description: PURL of the package without the version component.

reasons.description: Reasons for flagging the package as malicious.

references.description: Reference URLs for the malware record.

upsert_key.description:
The upsert key of the malware record. This will be ecosystem+package_name_version for specific version type records.
For range type records, it will be ecosystem+package_name.

v1MalwareWorkflowLLMConfig.description: MalwareWorkflowLLMConfig carries the LLM-specific settings for a signal that is backed by a language model.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of output tokens the model may generate.

model.description: Model identifier used for inference, e.g. "vertex_ai/gemini-2.0-flash".

prompt_template.description: Go template name to render the prompt; defaults to the signal class default when absent.

save_prompt.description: When true, the rendered prompt is persisted alongside the assessment for audit and replay.

v1MalwareWorkflowLLMConfigThinkingLevel.description:
ThinkingLevel controls the depth of reasoning a model applies before producing a response.

 - THINKING_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED: No thinking level has been set; the model uses its default behavior.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_AUTO: The model selects the appropriate thinking depth automatically.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_LOW: Minimal reasoning; faster and cheaper, suited for straightforward signals.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_MEDIUM: Moderate reasoning; balanced between quality and cost.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_HIGH: Maximum reasoning; slower and more expensive, suited for complex verdicts.

v1MavenSpec.description: MavenSpec represents a configuration for the Maven package manager.

id.description:
A string that uniquely identifies this proxy/server. This is the
UUID of the object if not provided.

is_plugin_repository.description: Indicates whether the repository is a plugin or binary repository.

name.description:
User identifiable name for the repository. This is the name
of the package manager if not provided.

password.description:
An encrypted password that must be provided by the repository owner.
Superseded by `auth`; kept only for migration, removed in a later CR.

priority.description:
The priority of the Maven package manager.
Priorities are relative. If multiple package managers
have the same priority, the order between them can be random.
Lower number means higher priority.

public_repository.description: Indicates if cloud storage is accessible publicly.

region.title: Region to be used for cloud storage integration

snapshots.description: Indicates whether the repository can contain snapshot versions.

url.description: The URL of the registry that the Maven package manager must use.

user.description:
The user name to use to access this repo.
Superseded by `auth`; kept only for migration, removed in a later CR.

v1McpDimensionThresholds.description:
McpDimensionThresholds holds per-dimension score thresholds for
McpServerActivity. Each field is optional; an unset dimension is ignored.
Set dimensions are OR'd among themselves and with score_at_or_below:
any single dimension at or below its threshold fires the predicate.
Dimension names mirror AgenticInventory.McpScoreDimensions.

authentication_authorization.description:
Threshold for authentication & authorization (credential-less network
access, hardcoded secrets).

input_validation_injection.description:
Threshold for input validation & injection (shell/SQL/code injection,
prompt-poisoning patterns).

operational_hygiene.description:
Threshold for operational hygiene (spec conformance, destructive tool
labeling).

supply_chain_provenance.description:
Threshold for supply chain & provenance (malicious packages, CVEs,
unverified publishers, unpinned deps).

v1McpServerActivity.description:
McpServerActivity matches MCP servers by name patterns and/or score
thresholds. Match logic: configured branches are AND'd — when both
server_name_matchers and score predicates are set, both must hold;
when only one is set, only that one must hold; if neither is set,
the activity never matches. Within the score branch, score_at_or_below
and every set field of dimension_at_or_below are OR'd: any single
satisfied threshold fires the branch. This is server-level matching;
for per-tool-call matching, use McpToolCallActivity.

score_at_or_below.description:
Match when the overall score is at or below this threshold
(scores are 1-10, higher = safer). OR'd with dimension_at_or_below.

server_name_matchers.description:
Regex matchers for MCP server name (e.g. "untrusted-.*", "remote-.*").
AND'd with the score-predicate branch when both are configured.

v1McpServerMatch.description:
McpServerMatch describes an MCP server that matched a policy. Carries
only the matched server's name; consumers can fetch the full McpMeta
from AgenticInventory if more detail is needed. Server-level match;
for individual tool calls, see McpToolMatch.

mcp_server_name.description: Name of the MCP server that matched.

message.description:
Describes what exactly matched (e.g. "score at or below threshold 5",
"supply_chain_provenance at or below 4").

v1McpServerSource.description:
McpServerSource is where an MCP server came from. Orthogonal to ServerType,
which answers "where does it run": a vendor connector is a connector by
source and REMOTE by type at the same time. Declared here rather than in
agentic_inventory.proto because that file imports this one, not the reverse.

 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED: Not classified: no config snapshot was available to check the server
against. Distinct from "checked and absent", which is CLIENT_INJECTED.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_PROJECT_CONFIG: Registered in the workspace's own checked-in agent config.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_USER_CONFIG: Registered in the user's home-directory agent config.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_ENTERPRISE_CONFIG: Registered in the OS-managed enterprise agent config.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_PLUGIN: Supplied by an agent plugin's manifest rather than by an mcp_servers entry.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_VENDOR_CONNECTOR: Vendor hosted connector enabled on the user's agent account, for
example a claude.ai connector. Never present in local config.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_CLIENT_RESERVED: A name the client reserves for one of its own built in servers, so
user config cannot register under it. Highest confidence verdict.
 - MCP_SERVER_SOURCE_CLIENT_INJECTED: Injected by the client at runtime but not on the reserved list: other
product surfaces, IDE bridges, host applications. Absent from a config
snapshot that was loaded.

v1McpToolCallActivity.description: McpToolCallActivity matches tool calls to a specific MCP server and tool.

server_name_matchers.description: Optional regex matchers for MCP server name.

tool_input_matchers.description: Optional regex matchers for tool input (e.g. ".*AI.*").

tool_name_matchers.description: Optional regex matchers for tool name.

v1McpToolHook.description: McpToolHook contains payload for MCP tool-related hooks.

cmd_line.description:
Shell command this call runs, when the tool is a shell (Claude Desktop's
local agent mode exposes server "workspace", tool "bash"). Such a call is
indistinguishable in what it can do from the agent's own Bash tool, but the
command arrives inside tool_input, where nothing that reads CmdHook.cmd_line
can find it. Lifting it here gives the two paths one field to read, so a
consumer does not have to re-derive the shell-tool vocabulary to see the
highest-signal action an agent takes. Empty for every non-shell tool.

server_host.description: Host or URL of the server (e.g. "localhost", "https://api.example.com").

tool_input.description: Tool invocation input; structure is tool-specific (use Struct for JSON).

tool_response.description: Tool result; structure is tool-specific (e.g. stdout/stderr or filenames).

v1McpToolMatch.description: McpToolMatch describes a tool call that matched a policy.

v1Meta.description: Common fields for all Endor Labs resources.

annotations.description:
Annotations can be used to attach metadata to a resource message.
Annotation values can be small or large, structured or unstructured,
and may include characters not permitted by labels.
The keys may contain alphanumerics, underscores (_), dots (.) and dashes
(-). The values of an annotation must be 16384 bytes or smaller.

create_time.description:
Time the resource was created.

Format: 2017-01-15T01:30:15.01Z
RFC 3339: https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt.

created_by.description:
Name and authentication source of the user who created the object,
for example, ewok@endor.ai@google@api-key.

description.description: Resource description. Must be less than 1024 bytes.

kind.description:
Resource kind, for example, HelloResponse.
Auto-generated using the protobuf message proto.MessageName().Name().

name.description: Resource name. Must be 63 characters or less.

parent_kind.description: Parent object resource kind, for example, Project.

references.description: Map of objects referenced in a query API.

tags.description:
List of tags attached to the resource.
Tags can be used to select objects and to find collections of objects that
satisfy certain conditions. A tag must be 255 characters or less.

update_time.description:
Time the resource was last updated.
Note: Updated on all create/patch/delete operations.

Format: 2017-01-15T01:30:15.01Z
RFC 3339: https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt.

updated_by.description:
Name and authentication source of the last user who updated the object,
for example, vulnerabilityingestor@endor.ai@x509.

upsert_time.description:
Time the resource was last upserted.

Note:
create_time is only set the first time the resource is created.
upsert_time is set every time the resource is upseted.

Format: 2017-01-15T01:30:15.01Z
RFC 3339: https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt.

version.description: Message version.

v1Method.description:
The type of allowed action.

 - METHOD_READ: METHOD_READ is for LIST/GET
 - METHOD_CREATE: METHOD_CREATE is for POST
 - METHOD_UPDATE: METHOD_UPDATE is for PATCH
 - METHOD_DELETE: METHOD_DELETE is for DELETE
 - METHOD_ALL: METHOD_ALL is for all methods (essentially *)

v1MetricConfiguration.description: This message contains the definition all metrics configurations.

uuid.description: The UUID of the metric.

v1MetricConfigurationSpec.description: The internal specification of the metric configuration.

category.description: The categories of metrics available for this kind.

enabled.description: Whether this metric is enabled in the current configuration or not.

options.description:
The parameteres used for the calculations. This is
a read only object at this time.

type.description: Type is the kind of metric available.

analytic.description: The name of the analytic used to generate this specific metric.

metric_values.description:
A map of metric values.
These values include scores and score factors.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project to which this metric relates.

raw.description: This is a superset of the information included in the specification.

v1MetricValue.description: The value of the metric and the associated category.

external_installation_id.description:
Endor Labs Hugging Face installation ID of this project.
Optional and only available if the project is created through an installation.

full_name.description:
The author and model name.
For example, author/model_name.

http_clone_url.description:
The HTTP clone URL of the project.
For example, https://huggingface.co/openai-community/gpt2.

v1NPMSpec.description: NPMSpec represents a configuration for the Node package manager.

auth_token.description:
An auth token that cloud providers typically provide to connect to the
registry.

priority.description:
The priority of the Node package manager.
Priorities are relative. If multiple package managers
have the same priority, the order between them can be random.
Lower number means higher priority.

scope.title:
A private registry scope.
Ex: @myorg/pkg
myorg is the scope

token.description: A base64 encoded user name and password as token.

url.description: The URL of the registry that NPM must use.

v1NVDVulnerability.description:
NVD Vulnerability.
Based on schema definition provided by NVD here. https://csrc.nist.gov/schema/nvd/api/2.0/cve_api_json_2.0.schema.

v1Namespace.description:
Namespace provides a mechanism for isolating groups of resources.
Namespaces may be defined in a parent child hierarchy.

uuid.description: The UUID of a namespace.

full_name.description:
The fully qualified name of a namespace,
which identifies the namespace and the associated
hierarchy. For example, endord.dev.domain.
The field is auto-generated at creation.

managed.description: Managed indicates that the object is managed by the system.

v1Notification.description: The record created when there is a policy violation.

uuid.description: The UUID of a notification.

error_status.description: Error provided by the notification action.

is_ignored.description: Is the notification ignored by the plugin.

last_failed_at.description: Timestamp of the last failed action attempt, used for exponential backoff.

open_action_complete.description: The value is true when action related to opening a new notification action is successfully executed.

resolve_action_complete.description: The value is true when action related to resolving an notification is successfully executed.

retry_count.description: Number of times the action has been retried after failure.

update_action_complete.description: The value is true when action related to updating an existing notification is successfully executed.

notification_target_uuid.description: The UUID of the notification target which contains the action to be performed for the notification.

v1NotificationPluginOperation.description:
- NOTIFICATION_PLUGIN_OPERATION_OPEN: Corresponds to creating a new notification.
 - NOTIFICATION_PLUGIN_OPERATION_UPDATE: Corresponds to updating an existing notification.
 - NOTIFICATION_PLUGIN_OPERATION_RESOLVE: Corresponds to resolving a notification.

finding_details.description: The map of finding UUID to finding object.

hashsum.description:
The SHA-256 hash sum of the notification payload.
The notification payload is a list of UUIDs (of say Findings/Metrics) and/or
an opaque blob. The list of UUIDs and the opaque data is used as input for the hashing function.

The hashsum is used to determine if the latest notification payload has changed
so as to update the notification target when there is a change.

last_seen_at.description: The time when the notification was last raised.

notification_action_data.description:
A map of metadata related to the notification action, indexed by the notification target UUID.

It maintains the following information related to every notification target.

- Flags to determine if an action related to a notification target
  is successfully completed or not.  If not, the action
  is retried in subsequent attempts. Flags are maintained for
  actions related to OPEN/UPDATE/RESOLVE.
- Metadata specific to a notification target type. Some of
  the notification target types need to maintain state so that
  subsequent updates to the notifications can operate on the
  same entity created by the notification. For example, JIRA

  hence the need to store JIRA ID.

v1PackageFirewallAction.description:
PackageFirewallAction defines how the package firewall responds when a check is triggered.
Used in both configuration (what to do) and audit logs (what was done).

 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_ACTION_BLOCK: Block the request and return HTTP 403.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_ACTION_WARN: Log a warning audit event and allow the request to proceed.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_ACTION_CURATED: One or more versions were removed from the package metadata response as part of package curation.
The package manager resolves to the best remaining safe version without seeing the curated-out versions.

v1PackageFirewallCheckFailureCause.description:
PackageFirewallCheckFailureCause identifies why a policy decision was unavailable.

 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_CHECK_FAILURE_CAUSE_UNSPECIFIED: No safe failure cause was recorded.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_CHECK_FAILURE_CAUSE_POLICY_DATASTORE_UNAVAILABLE: Firewall configuration could not be read from the policy datastore.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_CHECK_FAILURE_CAUSE_MALWARE_DATA_UNAVAILABLE: Malware status could not be read for the requested package version.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_CHECK_FAILURE_CAUSE_POLICY_EVALUATION_ERROR: A configured policy check could not complete its evaluation or query.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_CHECK_FAILURE_CAUSE_UPSTREAM_METADATA_UNAVAILABLE: Supporting upstream package metadata could not be fetched or transformed.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_CHECK_FAILURE_CAUSE_UPSTREAM_METADATA_NOT_FOUND: Supporting upstream package metadata did not contain the requested package or version.

v1PackageFirewallLog.description:
PackageFirewallLog represents a package firewall audit event recording the
action taken and the reason that triggered it.

uuid.description: The UUID of the package firewall log.

action_at.description: Timestamp when the firewall action (block or warn) occurred.

api_key_id.description: API key ID used for the request (for audit purposes).

api_key_name.title: Human-readable name of the API key (APIKey.meta.name) used for the request

configured_fail_closed.description: Configured failure behavior at evaluation time (populated only when reason is POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED).

cvss_vuln_uuid.description: UUID of the Vuln object for the highest-severity vulnerability detected (populated only when reason is CVSS_SEVERITY_DETECTED).

filtered_versions.description:
Per-version detail for MetadataAllVersions curation events.
Populated when package_curation_enabled = true and one or more versions were suppressed
from the metadata response because their per-policy action is BLOCK. Empty for all other request types.

malware_uuid.description: UUID of detected malware (populated only when reason is MALWARE_DETECTED).

min_age_hours.description:
Configured minimum age threshold in hours, snapshotted from PackageFirewallConfig.min_age_hours
at evaluation time (populated only when reason is MIN_AGE_NOT_MET). Combine with action_at and
package_age_hours to derive when the package becomes eligible.

package_age_hours.description: Age of package in hours (populated only when reason is MIN_AGE_NOT_MET).

package_license.description: License of the package (populated only when reason is RESTRICTED_LICENSE).

package_version.description: Version of the blocked package (if available).

remote_address.description: The remote IP address that made the request.

request_type.description: Type of request that was blocked (metadata, download, etc.).

request_uri.description: URI of the request that was blocked.

restricted_license.description:
Configured restricted license string that matched and caused this event, snapshotted from
PackageFirewallConfig.restricted_licenses at evaluation time (populated only when reason is RESTRICTED_LICENSE).

user.description: Client-supplied user attribution decoded from the Basic-auth username (e.g. user/machine); free-form and unverified.

v1PackageFirewallReason.description:
PackageFirewallReason represents the check that triggered the firewall event.

 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_MALWARE_DETECTED: Malware was detected in the requested package version.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_MIN_AGE_NOT_MET: The requested package version does not meet the configured minimum age.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_RESTRICTED_LICENSE: The requested package version has a license that is on the restricted list.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_CVSS_SEVERITY_DETECTED: The requested package version has a CVSS vulnerability meeting or exceeding the configured severity threshold.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_VERSIONS_CURATED: One or more versions were removed from the package metadata response as part of package curation.
See PackageFirewallLog.Spec.filtered_versions for per-version detail.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED: The configured policy could not produce a decision for the package request.

v1PackageLicenseOverride.description:
PackageLicenseOverride represents user edits and selections for licenses, copyrights, and notices
at the package version level. Edits made at this level apply across all projects in the namespace
that use the same package version.
The package version UUID is stored in spec.package_version_uuid.

propagate.description:
Indicates whether this override should be visible in child namespaces.
When querying from a descendant namespace, handlers should include parent
overrides only when this flag is set to true (same inheritance pattern as policies).

uuid.description: The UUID of the package license override.

copyright_overrides.description:
Map of copyright key to CopyrightOverride.
Contains copyrights that have been edited or newly added by the user.
Original copyrights from PackageLicense are NOT stored here - they are fetched from PackageLicense when needed.
Key format:
  - For edited copyrights from PackageLicense: use the key from PackageLicense.spec.copyrights map.
    (this is the file path where the copyright was found).
  - For new copyrights added by user: use generated UUID prefixed with "new-".

deselected_copyrights.description:
Map of copyright key to selection state.
Only deselected copyrights are stored here (value = false).
If a copyright key is not present in this map, it defaults to selected (true).

deselected_licenses.description:
Map of license identifier to selection state.
Only deselected licenses are stored here (value = false).
If a license identifier is not present in this map, it defaults to selected (true).

deselected_notices.description:
Map of notice identifier to selection state.
Only deselected notices are stored here (value = false).
If a notice identifier is not present in this map, it defaults to selected (true).

license_overrides.description:
Map of license identifier to LicenseOverride.
Contains licenses that have been edited or newly added by the user.
Original licenses from PackageLicense are NOT stored here - they are fetched from PackageLicense when needed.
Key format: hash calculated from normalized license text (same calculation as PackageLicenseInfo.hash).
  - For edited licenses from PackageLicense: use hash from PackageLicenseInfo.hash.
    (this hash maps to the key in PackageLicense.spec.license_text map).
  - For new licenses added by user: calculate hash from the license_text provided in LicenseOverride.
    The hash is calculated using the same method: SHA256(MakeLicenseKey(normalized_license_text)).
The hash is calculated from the normalized license text and is available for all
license types (code_licenses, package_manager_licenses, declared_code_licenses).

notice_overrides.title:
Map of notice identifier to NoticeOverride.
Contains notices that have been edited or newly added by the user.
Original notices from PackageLicense are NOT stored here - they are fetched from PackageLicense when needed.
Key format:
  - For edited notices from PackageLicense: use hash or composite identifier
  - For new notices added by user: use generated UUID prefixed with "new-"

v1Policy.description: Policy represents a policy in the system.

propagate.description: Whether the object should be visible in child namespaces or not.

uuid.description: The UUID of the policy.

v1PolicyIntent.description:
PolicyIntent says what kind of rule a policy encodes, and so whether the LLM
command judge may rule on its matches. Only cmd_line policies are judged, so
today the intent changes behavior only on a cmd_line policy.

 - POLICY_INTENT_UNSPECIFIED: Read as POLICY_INTENT_RISK, so a policy that never sets the field keeps the
behavior it had before the field existed.
 - POLICY_INTENT_RISK: The policy is a risk assessment. A judge scope may hand its matches to the
judge, and the label can release, ask about, or block the command.
 - POLICY_INTENT_GOVERNANCE: The policy is an organisational rule, for example "installs go through the
package firewall". A verdict on how risky the command is answers a question
the rule does not ask, so no judge scope hands its matches to the judge.
Its own action is final: no label releases it, and no label escalates it.
Not valid with the AUTO action, which hands the decision to the judge.

bypass_exceptions.description:
Set to true if exception policies should be ignored for findings
matching this policy.

notification_target_uuids.description:
The list of UUIDs of the notification targets that are configured for
this policy.

standalone_tickets.description:
Set to true to create every tracker ticket as a standalone ticket with
no parent. When false, aggregated tickets are created as child issues
under one parent ticket.

allow.description:
True if input data is accepted by policy.
False if input data violates the expected state.

violating_resources.description:
Lists of UUIDs of resources that violate the policy,
if applicable, indexed by resource name.

disable.description: Disables a policy without deleting it.

finding_categories.description:
List of finding categories that the policy creates or acts on findings
for. This field can be used to group policies.

group_by_fields.description:
Custom fields to group policy output by. This may be a
subset of all custom keys in the policy output. You do not need to
add all custom fields here, just the ones you want to be used to
group the matches by. The corresponding values
are always treated as a single string.

project_exceptions.description:
The set of tags that projects that are matched
with are excluded from the policy. Allows exceptions. Exceptions
can be provided with or without selectors.

project_selector.description:
The set of tags that projects must have for the policy to be executed
against. If left empty, the policy applies to all projects of the
namespace. The items in the array correspond to an OR operator. That is,
any project with a tag that matches any of the project_selector values
will be matched.

query_statements.description:
The list of OPA query statements that must be executed to evaluate the
policy. For example, [ "data.packagename.allow" ], [opulated from
template if applicable.

resource_kinds.description:
Identifies all resources that a policy requires.
For example, "Project", "Repository", "RepositoryVersion",
"PackageVersion", "DependencyMetadata", "Metric", "LinterResult",
"Finding", etc. For the "Metric" resource you must also specify the
corresponding parent resource kind.

rule.description:
The policy rule in text format.

For example:

package policyexample

default allow = false

allow {
   data.resources.Project[_].meta.name = go-memdb"
}

template_parameters.description: Template parameter metadata for this template version.

template_uuid.description: Indicates that the policy is created from a template.

template_values.description: The map of key-value pairs for parameters used to customize the template.

templates can be used to create policies from these templates.

(unless Policy.AutoEnable is explicitly disabled in SystemConfig).

if this flag is set to true.

deprecated.description:
Set to True if the policy template has been deprecated.
Policies created from deprecated templates are never deleted,
but the template is no longer visible in the UI.

finding_categories.description:
List of finding categories that the policy creates or acts on findings
for. This field can be used to group policy templates.

group_by_fields.description:
Custom fields to group policy output by. This may be a subset of all
custom keys in the policy output. You do not need to add all custom
fields here. You can add just the custom fileds you want to be used to
group the matches by. The corresponding values are always treated as a
single string.

The list of OPA query statements that must be executed to evaluate the
resulting policy. For example, [ "data.packagename.allow" ].

release_notes.description: Release notes indexed by template version.

resource_kinds.description:
The additional resources that a policy requires.
By default, policies are executed against Project, Repository,
RepositoryVersion, PackageVersion, Metric and Finding. If a policy
must include additional objects they must be defined here.

rule.description:
The policy template rule in text format.

For example:

package policyexample

default allow = false

allow {
   input.Value1 = input.Value2
}

template_parameters.description:
The list of values to customize the template. In the example above,
Value1 and Value2.

with are excluded from the policy. Allows exceptions. Exceptions
can be provided with or without selectors.

project_selector.title:
The set of tags that projects must have for the policy to be executed against. If left empty, the policy
applies to all projects of the namespace. The items in the array
correspond to an OR operator. (ie any project with a tag that matches any
of the project_selector values will be matched.)

project_uuid.description: The UUID of project to load data from [optional].

query_statements.description:
List of OPA query statements that must be executed to

v1Query.description: Query implements the metric query requests.

uuid.description: The UUID of the resource.

v1QueryCommandClassification.description:
QueryCommandClassification labels a shell command an AI coding agent proposed
to run: benign, suspicious, or review. The judgment is made on the command's
own security intent and effect, with no pattern behind it, which is what lets
it stand in for the CMD_LINE regexes rather than only second-guess them.

The caller sends the command and nothing else. The prompt, the model, and the
judging rubric all live on the server, which is what keeps this endpoint
different in kind from AIRequest: a caller cannot choose the model or steer
the prompt, so the capability it grants is "classify a command", not "run
inference on this tenant's account". That is the same split that lets AIQuery
be safe for read-only callers.

uuid.description: The uuid of the resource.

v1QueryCommandClassificationLabel.description:
Label is the judgment on one command. Each value maps to an action the
agent hook already has.

 - LABEL_UNSPECIFIED: No label was produced. Never treat this as a benign result.
 - LABEL_BENIGN: The command shows nothing concerning on its own.
 - LABEL_SUSPICIOUS: The command shows something concerning.
 - LABEL_REVIEW: The decision turns on context the model does not have, so the command
belongs in front of the user rather than being cleared or blocked.

v1QueryCommandClassificationSpec.description:
Spec carries the one input and the judgment, plus what the call cost. The
caller sends command and reads everything else back.

ai_request_uuid.description:
Uuid of the AIRequest row this classification was billed as. That row
carries CompletionUsage and the credit accounting, so it is the join key
for deriving what a judgment cost; the caller stores the uuid rather than
a currency figure, which would go stale on a price change.

cached_tokens.description:
Tokens served from the provider's prompt cache. The rubric is a standing
prefix, so this reports whether it is actually being cached.

command.description:
The command to judge, as the hook observed it. It is judged on its own
security intent and effect: no policy, pattern, or action tier is sent,
because there may not have been one.

completion_tokens.description:
Tokens the label itself cost. Small by design: the answer is one JSON
object, so a large value here means the model is explaining itself.

confidence.description:
Confidence in the label, 0.0 to 1.0. Advisory only: it is reported so a
threshold can be calibrated against real data rather than guessed.

deployment_context.description:
Free-text lines describing the caller's deployment: which hosts are the
organisation's own, which registries are sanctioned, which credentials are
expected to be present on the machine.

They fill the trust anchors the rubric names as deployment-supplied and
ships empty, and they are appended AFTER the rubric so the rubric stays a
byte-identical standing prefix the provider can serve from its cache.

This is the one input besides the command, and it is still not a prompt:
the caller supplies facts about its environment, not instructions to the
model. It comes from the tenant's own auto-mode policy rather than from
the hook's own reading of the machine.

model.description:
The model that produced the label, for attribution and for comparing one
model against another.

prompt_tokens.description:
Tokens the classification consumed. The caller runs this in the critical
path of a developer's agent, so it is told what the call cost.

reason.description: One clause naming the concrete thing seen in the command.

rubric_version.description:
Version of the rubric the label was produced under. A label recorded today
is not comparable to one recorded after the rubric changed, so the caller
is told which one judged its command rather than having to assume.

v1ScanCreditUsage.description:
ScanCreditUsage is a per-tenant snapshot of scan credit consumption produced
by the licensing aggregation job. One object is written per aggregation run
covering a fixed [period_start, period_end) window. The most recent object's
term_* fields hold cumulative usage for the current contract term anchored
at EndorLicense.spec.credits_period_start.

uuid.description: The UUID of the scan credit usage record.

credits_period_start.description:
Anchor timestamp of the current contract term. Snapshotted from
EndorLicense.spec.credits_period_start at aggregation time so historic
rows remain interpretable after renewal.

cumulative_scan_credits.description:
Cumulative credits consumed since credits_period_start through
window_end. Sum of all six cumulative_breakdown counters. Used to
render remaining credits and overage in the UI without rescanning all
snapshots.

onboarded_project_count.description:
Number of non-deleted projects onboarded under the tenant observed at
aggregation time. Used to decide whether the 5x-seats default-branch cap
was exceeded.

overflow_project_count.description:
Number of projects beyond the 5x-seats cap whose default-branch scans
contributed to *_main_overflow_credits counters. Zero when
onboarded_project_count <= 5 * seats.

scan_credit_limit.description:
Scan credit limit in effect at aggregation time. Snapshotted from
EndorLicense.spec.scan_credit_limit. Overage = max(0, cumulative_scan_credits - credit_limit).

window_end.description:
End of the aggregation window this snapshot covers (exclusive). All
ScanResults with create_time in [window_start, window_end) contributed
to window_* fields.

window_scan_credits.description:
Total credits consumed during [window_start, window_end). Sum of all
six window_breakdown counters.

window_start.description:
Start of the aggregation window this snapshot covers (inclusive).
Typically equals the previous run's window_end, or term_start for the
first run of a term.

v1ScanState.description:
Scan state for a project or package version.

 - SCAN_STATE_NOT_PROCESSED: Object has not been processed by the system yet.
Set when the project or package is created for the first time.
A new project or package version is automatically placed in this state.
 - SCAN_STATE_IDLE: Object has been scanned at least once.
 - SCAN_STATE_INGESTING: Object is being scanned.
 - SCAN_STATE_ANALYTIC: Object is being analyzed.
 - SCAN_STATE_UNREACHABLE: Object cannot be ingested because it is not reachable from the scheduler.
 - SCAN_STATE_REQUEST_FULL_RESCAN: Object is marked for a complete rescan.
This only applies to OSS projects.
 - SCAN_STATE_REQUEST_INCREMENTAL_RESCAN: Object is marked for an incremental rescan, where only new packages
discovered in the scan are added. Indicates that this project should be
rescanned with a higher priority. Often because it is used by a customer
and we need any new packages to be discovered and scanned with higher
priority. If the project is put in this state, we will scan any new
packages at high priority but we will not re-scan older packages.
 - SCAN_STATE_QUEUED: Object is queued to be scanned.
 - SCAN_STATE_QUARANTINED: Scan scheduling was unsuccessful due to a system errors. Object is
quarantined from additional scheduling. Potentially object is an
orphan or similar situations.

SchedulerResourceHistory stores per-project resource usage history and sizing

size the next run's resource requests.

the current sizing recommendation derived from that history.

v1ScopePolicy.description:
ScopePolicy represents a scope policy in the system. Scope policies allow users
to select for a set of projects (or namespaces) as defined by the project selectors.
It is the set of policies that are applied to these projects as defined by a policy selector.

uuid.description: The UUID of a scope policy.

excluded_project_tag_selector.description: The set of tags that projects must not have for the scope policy to be executed against.

policy_namespace_selector.description:
Selects all policies in the namespace to be applied.
If the policy_namespace_selector is defined, the policy_tag_selector cannot be defined at the same time.
For example, defining a policy_namespace_selector of "tenant" will indicate that all policies
in the tenant must be applied to the projects defined with the above selectors.

policy_tag_selector.description: The set of tags that policies must match to be applied to a project.

project_namespace_selector.description:
The list of namespaces for which this scope rule will apply.
For example, defining a namespace "tenant" will mean that the rule applies for all
projects in the namespace.

project_tag_selector.description:
The set of tags that projects must have for the scope policy to be executed against.
If left empty, the scope policy applies to all projects of the namespace. The items in the array
correspond to an OR operator. That is, any project with a tag that matches any
of the project_selector values will be matched.

v1ScoreCard.description: A scorecard contains a total score per ScoreCategory.

v1ScoreCategory.description:
The types of scores that Endor Labs tracks.

 - SCORE_CATEGORY_POPULARITY: Tracks a project's popularity.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_ACTIVITY: Tracks the amount of activity around a project.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_BEST_PRACTICES: Tracks how much a project follows various development best practices.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY: Tracks suspicious activity on a project.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_DEPENDENCIES: Tracks the dependencies of a project.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_SECURITY: Tracks security aspects of a project.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_CODE_QUALITY: Tracks the code quality of a project.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_OPERATIONAL_RISK: Tracks the operationa risk of a project.

v1ScoreFactor.description:
A score factor for an object. Each score factor
describes a piece of information used while computing the overall score.
Each factor is associated with a specific category. Score factors can have a
positive impact on the repository score and then they have a positive score, or can
have a negative impact on the overall score and then they have a positive score.
The description captures additional information for the particular factor.
In general there are many (tens or hundreds) of such score factors split across the ScoreCategory categories.

Postive score factor example:

 Category: SCORE_CATEGORY_BEST_PRACTICES

 Score: 2

 Description: The repository is enforcing signed commits.

Negative score factor example:

Category: SCORE_CATEGORY_VULNERABILITIES

Score: -1

Description: the repository has unresolved issues related to vulnerabilities that have been open for more than 3 months.

score_float.description: The float value of the score for the factor.

Internal specification of the object.

Follows the specification of the gitleaks configuration object defined
here: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/config/rule.go

allowlists.description:
Allows a rule to be ignored for specific regexes, paths, and/or commits.
Replaces the singular allowlist field to align with gitleaks v8.21+

independent regex_target and condition values.

A golang regular expression used to
filter secrets by path

git_log_scanned.description:

v1SecretsCheckActivity.description:
SecretsCheckActivity runs Endor's secret detection over file content (the
proposed content of a write/edit, or a file read scanned from disk). Matching
the activity means running the scan; the verdict comes from the findings, not
from the policy config.

exclude_file_patterns.description:
Skip files whose path matches one of these regexes (e.g. test fixtures,
"*.example" files, vendored dirs). Applied after include_file_patterns.

exclude_rule_ids.description:
Rule IDs whose findings this policy ignores. Matched as for
include_rule_ids, and applied after it, so an id in both is ignored.

file_operations.description:
File operations to scan. Empty means write and edit; scanning a read means
reading the file from disk, so reads are opt-in.

include_file_patterns.description:
Only scan files whose path matches one of these regexes. Empty means all
files the event covers.

include_rule_ids.description:
Rule IDs whose findings this policy acts on, compared exactly and
case-sensitively against the rule id on each finding
(SecretRule.spec.rule_id, e.g. "aws-access-token"). Empty means every rule in
the tenant's effective ruleset.

the rule and location, never the secret value, so a finding can be surfaced

A segment index request allows the caller to provide a set of code
segments with their associated metadata that should be indexed as part the
embeddings store. Embeddings are only created. They are only read through the
SegmentQueryRequest. The request can include multiple segments to allow
parallel execution.

Whether the client wants embedding vectors computed for the segments

this field existed keeps its current embedding behavior; only an

A segment query request allows the caller to send a set of segments and find
similarities based on the embeddings. Callers can send multiple segments in
one call. Caller provides the content and embeddings server responds with the
best file version matches.

One query per file.
Each query can contain metadata for multiple file segments.

Can be a tag, a branch or a SHA.

ServiceRequest defines a message for raising requests to perform resource updates

The list of approver email IDs to which this service request

slack_message_ts.title: Slack Message TimeStamp ("ts") of the notification, used to update the notification status

target_namespace.description: The resource namespace on which operations needs to be performed.

expiration_time for the token that should before the
